item.title: Lakers biggest test is coming, but it’s not Spurs, per JJ Redick
item.description: The Lakers’ biggest test of the season is coming up. It’s not Friday, when they’ll face Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs. It’s Saturday, when the world will be reacting to whatever transpired. “Whether we lose the game, whether we win the game, we’re either going to be contenders on [ESPN’s] ‘First Take’ or we’re not going to be contenders and we’re fake,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. “That stuff is just noise.” For the Lakers, their upcoming game against the Spurs is a temperature check. The teams are tied for the best record in the NBA at 15-3 . And their stars, Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama, are in a two-man race for the MVP Award. In other words, this is prime theater. And we all know what that means. San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama dunks against the Portland Trail Blazers in Portland, Ore., Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. AP Photo/Craig Mitchelldyer If the Lakers win, they’ll be the front-runners for the title . Doncic will officially be ahead of Wembanyama in the MVP race. The darlings of the NBA will be the crown jewel of the basketball world. But if they lose, well, the opposite will happen. There will be some version of sound the alarm. Press the panic button. The Lakers aren’t elite. Doncic isn’t the real deal. Walker Kessler can’t compete against the league’s top centers. So, the Lakers’ biggest test isn’t going to be whether they win a game in November. It’s going to be whether they can ignore the inevitable chatter when it becomes deafening. And it’s about to be dialed up to a feverish pitch. Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers handles the ball against the Utah Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images That’s what happens when the two top teams in the league meet, especially when one of those teams is the Lakers, who are arguably under a more powerful magnifying glass than any other franchise in the league. It’s fun to talk about the Lakers. They’ve won 17 championships. They’ve had some of the biggest stars in NBA history, including Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Magic Johnson, Kobe Bryant, LeBron James and Doncic. They’re a globally recognized brand. When they win, they’re the talk of the town. When they lose, the sky is falling. They inspire overreactions. They’re the dream fodder for pundits. That’s where things get interesting. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick watches his players during an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz in Los Angeles, Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong There are nine new players on the Lakers. They haven’t experienced the weight of that attention. It can be paralyzing. Even Doncic, who has been in the spotlight for most of his life , has never been the face of a franchise as big as the Lakers. This will be a major test. If the Lakers play great, they can’t let it get to their heads. And if they fall apart, they need to dust their shoulders and move forward. Championship teams lose games. But they don’t allow themselves to be defined

item.title: Week 12 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Germie Bernard vs. Courtland Sutton
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to take on the Denver Broncos amid a turbulent week for the team , but wideout Germie Bernard raises a compelling start case for Week 12 fantasy lineups. Courtland Sutton, one of Denver's top wideouts , also presents a solid fantasy outlook this week, with both him and Bernard forming the toughest start-sit debate for Black Friday's AFC clash. Bernard and the Steelers will be without four-time MVP Aaron Rodgers, who was released by the team after comments regarding head coach Mike McCarthy. The Case For Courtland Sutton Denver Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton against the Arizona Cardinals | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Before a quiet Week 11 performance against the Las Vegas Raiders, Sutton was in the midst of his best stretch of the season. From Week 7 to Week 9, the veteran wideout eclipsed 45 yards in every game, including a 15.5-point PPR performance in Week 9. The Steelers' defense has already allowed five different 70-yard receivers to this point in the season, and with volume closer to Week 9 than that of Week 11, Sutton could be in for another top-20 finish among fantasy wideouts this week. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 24th in pass defense so far this year, notably elevating Sutton's ceiling. The Case Against Sutton Sutton raised significant concerns among fantasy managers with a catchless outing against the Raiders last week. He was targeted just twice and took to social media to voice his concerns regarding his volume in Week 11. Without a reliable target share, it's hard for any receiver to sustain consistent production, a trend that could hamper Sutton's fantasy output once again this week. The Case For Courtland Sutton Denver Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton against the Arizona Cardinals | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Before a quiet Week 11 performance against the Las Vegas Raiders, Sutton was in the midst of his best stretch of the season. From Week 7 to Week 9, the veteran wideout eclipsed 45 yards in every game, including a 15.5-point PPR performance in Week 9. The Steelers' defense has already allowed five different 70-yard receivers to this point in the season, and with volume closer to Week 9 than that of Week 11, Sutton could be in for another top-20 finish among fantasy wideouts this week. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 24th in pass defense so far this year, notably elevating Sutton's ceiling. The Case Against Sutton Sutton raised significant concerns among fantasy managers with a catchless outing against the Raiders last week. He was targeted just twice and took to social media to voice his concerns regarding his volume in Week 11. Without a reliable target share, it's hard for any receiver to sustain consistent production, a trend that could hamper Sutton's fantasy output once again this week. The Case For Germie Bernard Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bernard has reached greater fantasy heights than Sutton this season, but has cooled off over recent weeks. The rookie wideout ranks second on the team in targets, coming off a Week 11 contest in which Bernard saw a team-high 10 looks in the passing game and notched his third week of double-digit fantasy scoring. Given his role as one of Pittsburgh's biggest RAC (run-after-catch) threats, he should see plenty of volume despite outside factors that could hamper the entire offense. The Case Against Bernard The Steelers' offense will take the field without Rodgers for the first time this season, thrusting veteran backup Mason Rudolph into the QB1 role for Week 12. It's hard to project how Pittsburgh's passing game will perform against a Broncos defense that has struggled this season, allowing 240 or more passing yards in five games. The Rudolph start is the biggest factor working against Bernard's Week 12 fantasy outlook in our start-sit debate, which will slightly affect our verdict. The Verdict Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard runs after a catch against the Green Bay Packers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Pittsburgh is in a bad way right now, but I'm still confident in Bernard's fantasy ceiling heading into a matchup against an inconsistent Broncos secondary. Sutton's production has been limited throughout the season, and Denver ranks just 19th in pass attempts while leaning on a potent rushing attack. I expect the Steelers' offense will be forced to lean on the passing game if the run game's struggles persist, which seems likely against a Broncos' run defense that has held teams under 100 yards in three of its last four games. item.title: Leverkusen return to winning ways in Europe with comfortable victory in Zagreb
item.description: Leverkusen return to winning ways in Europe with comfortable victory in Zagreb Bayer Leverkusen momentarily climbed to second in the Europa League standings after their comfortable win at GNK Dinamo Zagreb. Die Werkself have won four of their first five games in the competition as they only conceded a goal in their narrow defeat to Lyon. The hosts tested Mark Flekken inside the first minute with Lukas Kačavenda's effort. However, Carles Martinez's side were unfazed as they thoroughly dominated the rest of the half. The Dutch goalkeeper wasn't called into action since then, while Zagreb defenders had difficulties dealing with mazy wingers Ibrahim Maza and Moussa Diaby. Leverkusen took the lead from their first real chance with Malik Tillman's tenth goal for the club. Kacavenda saved Bruno Goda from scoring an own-goal, but the USMNT international was alert to tap it in from the rebound. A couple of minutes later, Dominik Kotarski made his first save of the game to deny Diaby. The Frenchman finished the half with a backheel assist as Jarell Quansah provided a superb finish to join Tillman in grabbing his second goal of the season. Having only conceded one goal in their first four fixtures, the visitors were in total control of the game to boost their chances of finishing in an automatic qualification spot for the Round of 16. Zagreb once again had the first attempt of the second-half right from the kick-off, but Josip Mišić's effort was off target. After lifeless ten minutes, both teams had great opportunities in space of few seconds. First, Leverkusen's goalscorer nearly combined for the third of the night before Quansah's shot narrowly missed the target. At the other end, former Augsburg striker and the leading goalscorer of the competition Dion Beljo was denied from close range by Flekken. With the upcoming big games domestically against Champions League clubs in mind, Martinez took off Maza and Patrik Schick around the hour mark. On his second appearance back from a long-term injury, substitute Chtistian Kofane came close to scoring Leverkusen's third before Diaby's strike from an offside position. The fullbacks Miguel Gutierrez and Quansah were also given a breather as Guela Duela makes his second appearance for the club after returning from an injury. Zagreb had their best spell of the game in the last 20 minutes, but Flekken didn't have to make more big saves in a comfortable evening for the 2023/24 finalists. Leverkusen will face Borussia Dortmund away from home in the last fixture of matchday 11 in Bundesliga before a midweek cup tie against RB Leipzig. Martinez's men will entertain Beşiktaş and RB Salzburg in Europa League before ending their league phase campaign at Lyon.

item.title: ‘You Don’t Do That to Your Teammates’ — Steelers Owner Art Rooney II ‘Disappointed’ With Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Decision After Benching
item.description: ‘You Don’t Do That to Your Teammates’ -- Steelers Owner Art Rooney II ‘Disappointed’ With Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Decision After Benching Aaron Rodgers is no longer a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After declaring that this was going to be his final season in the NFL, the four-time MVP was benched earlier in the week in a shocking move. Understandably, he did not take kindly to the news, going nuclear on head coach Mike McCarthy in particular about the way things unfolded. However, for owner and team president Art Rooney II, the actions from the former Super Bowl champion were disappointing. Art Rooney II Unimpressed With the Route Aaron Rodgers Took After the Steelers gave the starting job to Mason Rudolph for Week 12, and presumably beyond, Rodgers made an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” There, he had a ton of criticisms about McCarthy that he aired out publicly. From claiming that McCarthy was asleep during team meetings and not keeping up with film review to recounting the coach’s ‘1-2-3 Packers’ halftime gaffe, Rodgers aired a series of extraordinary criticisms of the veteran head coach. While some of the allegations were eye-opening, many people weren’t happy with the way Rodgers aired his dirty laundry. Rooney, who has been the team president for over two decades, was among those who did not support his actions. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette . “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure.” For Rooney, that broke a cardinal rule about team sports, as he added, “In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.” Then, he turned things around on Rodgers, calling him out for the way he had played so far in the season. Ranking at number 29 on PFN’s NFL Quarterback Impact metric, his QB Impact grade of 67.1 was by far the worst mark of his career. “The sad thing is, Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had. Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer It also showed up in consecutive weeks as they were blown out by the Cincinnati Bengals, a divisional rival, and lost to a Philadelphia Eagles team that had lost seven straight coming into their matchup. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.” Then, he turned things around on Rodgers, calling him out for the way he had played so far in the season. But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” It seems clear, from his release and now from Rooney’s comments, that the Steelers are done with Rodgers. Now, the interesting thing to note will be if a quarterback-needy team potentially decides to get into bed with him, if only for a short amount of time. item.title: Jim Nantz opens up on how J.J. Watt has ‘impressed’ him since his move to the CBS booth
item.description: Photo by Aaron Baker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt have already developed a great connection as broadcast partners for CBS. The former Houston Texans star was asked to replace Tony Romo by CBS in July, which meant that he did not have long to prepare for the season, but since he has started calling games, many have praised his analysis in the booth. After seeing how good Watt was alongside Nantz, CBS decided to sign the three-time Defensive Player of the Year to a multi-year contract. As they continue to navigate their way through their first season together, the legendary broadcaster has praised Watt for all his good work. Jim Nantz praises J.J. Watt’s preparation level for games While playing in the NFL, Watt had to do his homework, watch film, be a part of meetings, and speak to players. He continues to do all of this, but now as a member of the media. When he joined CBS, Watt had big shoes to fill, as Romo was one of the most loved voices. However, Nantz believes so far the five-time Pro Bowler has done a phenomenal job. “I think it’s been very good from the very beginning. I’m so excited about it. I’ve been extremely impressed by the way JJ conducts himself. When we talk about how we get ready for games, we hit people over the head about all the preparation that goes into it. I’m not sure that’s relatable to people who aren’t inside the business,” Nantz said in an interview with Front Office Sports. “I just can tell you briefly, from being on the inside, that he’s taken it to a level I’ve truly never seen before. It matches up, though, with who he is. He’s ready for anything. He’s not going to let anything surprise him. He fully has dissected every scenario and possibility in his head. He’s been a joy. There’s a lot of joyfulness, let’s just put it that way, in that booth right now.” A highlight for the duo was when Nantz tried to peanut-punch Watt to knock the ball out of his hands. Not only was the Hall of Fame broadcaster unable to get the ball out of Watt’s hands, but he also hurt himself in the process. The video of the incident went viral, with many asking Nantz if he was doing fine. Like every duo in the booth, Watt and Nantz seem to have found their groove. With CBS set to host the Super Bowl in 2028, the broadcaster will hope Watt keeps evolving and adds more to his skills in the booth. item.title: ‘That’s a Big Part of It’ — NFL Insider Reveals Commanders’ Stance on Brandon Aiyuk’s Mental Health After WR’s Reunion With Jayden Daniels
item.description: ‘That’s a Big Part of It’ — NFL Insider Reveals Commanders’ Stance on Brandon Aiyuk’s Mental Health After WR’s Reunion With Jayden Daniels The Brandon Aiyuk saga in San Francisco finally came to an end after two years. San Francisco finally released Aiyuk, and the long-term favorites to land him, the Washington Commanders, scooped him up to join his college quarterback, Jayden Daniels, in the nation’s capital. NFL insider Mike Garafolo recently detailed how the Commanders feel about their newest addition to their squad. Mike Garafolo Reveals Commanders’ Mindset on Signing Brandon Aiyuk Aiyuk hasn’t played a snap since October 2024. Just weeks before that season began, he signed a four-year, $120 million extension with San Francisco on Aug. 30, 2024, a deal that included $76 million in guarantees and was intended to keep him with the 49ers through 2028. After he suffered a season-ending injury in 2024, the relationship between Aiyuk and the 49ers reached a point of no return. He no longer had a role with the team and simply didn’t play. Eventually, they reached a resolution where the 49ers cut him after he was finally ready to play. item.title: Risacher Brings High-Energy Chaos To Mavericks Defense
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Zaccharie Risacher is not just playing; he is shaking up the entire Dallas roster with a style that only he can pull off. The 6-foot-8 wing has turned defensive intensity into the team’s most reliable spark plug this season. Per The Smoking Cuban , Risacher is averaging 9.1 points while posting career highs in rebounds, steals, and blocks. This is not the bad kind of chaos that hurts a season; it is the good kind that forces opponents to panic on every possession. A New Role for High Energy Dusty May has found the perfect spot for Risacher, letting him run wild rather than forcing him into a role he does not fit. He averages 2.9 deflections per game, a number that ranks second on the team behind only Cooper Flagg. Through 18 games, Risacher has thrown down 19 dunks, creating a direct path to offense with these actions. That average of 1.06 dunks per game is a career high for the young forward. Winning Without the Shot Falling The Mavericks have leaned heavily on this transition game because their half-court offense has struggled at times. By running past recovering defenders with his speed, Risacher finishes at the rim before the defense even sets up. Even when his outside shot is off, the team finds a way to score. Caleb Martin emphasized this mindset in an interview with Yardbarker following the win over Denver. Martin said the team must approach every game “as if it’s 0-0” because leads can vanish in the NBA. He noted that “when you stay locked in, no matter they make or miss,” the team stays engaged and ready. Over the last three games, Risacher has stepped up as a starter while shooting 53.3 percent from the field, averaging 12.7 points and 7.0 rebounds. His energy provides a spark that the Mavericks needed to break out of recent slumps. Martin told Yardbarker that the Mavericks “can still win games” even if their shots are not falling because they “can create offense from the defense.” The Dallas Mavericks are now 11-7 overall and 3-0 in the West Group A of the NBA Cup after their four-game winning streak. The Phoenix Suns face Dallas as its road trip continues on Friday.

item.title: ‘Should’ve Just Went to Miami,’ ‘Disrespectful to His Current Coach’ – NBA Fans React to LeBron James Praising Erik Spoelstra After 76ers-Heat
item.description: ‘Should’ve Just Went to Miami,’ ‘Disrespectful to His Current Coach’ – NBA Fans React to LeBron James Praising Erik Spoelstra After 76ers-Heat On Wednesday night, the Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Miami Heat 111-104. That win improved their record to 15-4. After the game, LeBron James had nothing but high praise for his opponent and former coach, Erik Spoelstra. LeBron James Had Nothing but Good Words for Erik Spoelstra During his postgame interview, James spoke warmly about Spoelstra and the lessons he took from their years together in Miami. “Spo is a first-ballot Hall of Famer. He’s one of the best coaches in our league. Obviously, the best coach I’ve had,” James said. James also talked about how he used to approach the game when he played under Spoelstra. “I didn’t want to be a guy who just went out there and ran and jumped. That’s a great quality and I found out I was gifted with that. But I’ve always had the IQ of a smart basketball player from the moment I picked up the game,” James added. The clip soon went viral, and the reaction from NBA fans followed almost immediately. MORE: ‘Objectively Not True,’ ‘Starts Off With a Lie and Somehow Gets Worse’ — NBA Fans Rip Bill Simmons Over Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Comparison There was a comment from a fan who suggested that, since James clearly holds Spoelstra and the Heat in such high regard, he should have gone back to Miami. They argued that after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers, James should have returned to the franchise where he won two championships rather than signing with the 76ers. “Man, he should’ve just went to Miami,” the fan wrote . Meanwhile, another user wrote , “Miss Spo and Bron hoops.” Another fan focused on the coach James plays for now. The fan claimed the statement was true but disrespectful to Nick Nurse, since James was effectively calling his old coach the best he has ever had. The fan wrote , “True statement but disrespectful as [expletive] to his current coach saying his old coach was the best coach he ever had.” The most pointed reaction brought up some uncomfortable history. Early in the 2010-11 season, shortly after James joined the Heat alongside Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh, the team stumbled to a 9-8 start amid chemistry issues and public scrutiny. Tension peaked after a loss to the Dallas Mavericks, when James reportedly bumped into Spoelstra on the sideline, and the players held a meeting that excluded the coach. According to accounts from team president Pat Riley, detailed years later in the book “The Soul of Basketball,” and from former teammate Eddie House, James and the other stars were unhappy with Spoelstra’s leadership. James even reportedly asked Riley whether he ever got “the itch” to coach again, which was widely interpreted as a subtle push for Riley to replace Spoelstra. item.title: Lions’ Amon-Ra St. Brown immediately trolls Ben Johnson with Stanky Leg celebration vs. Bears
item.description: Lions’ Amon-Ra St. Brown immediately trolls Ben Johnson with Stanky Leg celebration vs. Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Thursday afternoon, the Detroit Lions hit the field at home for a game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day. The game was a huge battle between NFC North titans, with both teams coming into this game riding some real momentum. Early on in this one, Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown reeled in an impressive catch down the field and immediately hit the Stanky Leg celebration, mimicking the move that Bears head coach Ben Johnson has done after wins throughout this season. Amon-Ra hit the stanky leg Ben Johnson after this one handed grab pic.twitter.com/GTyx8j6c7J Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) November 26, 2026 Johnson, of course, was the Lions’ offensive coordinator prior to taking the Bears’ head coaching job, and while fans in Detroit might respect the work he was able to do there, he isn’t exactly a fan favorite in the Motor City these days. Meanwhile, the top spot in the NFC North is seemingly wide open as the NFL season heads into its stretch run, with the Bears, Lions, Minnesota Vikings, and Green Bay Packers all fancying themselves legit contenders in the conference this year. The Lions ended up converting St. Brown’s big catch into a field goal to give themselves an early 3-0 lead over their division rivals. This game was also a rematch of the Thanksgiving matchup between Chicago and Detroit two years ago, in which the Bears pulled off one of the most stunning clock management blunders in NFL history en route to a loss, which ultimately opened the door for the firing that led to Johnson’s arrival. In any case, it appears that St. Brown has a bone to pick with his former OC. item.title: Embiid’s Absence Exposes A Fatal Flaw In The Sixers’ Plan
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers dropped a 128-111 decision to the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday night, a loss that ended a five-game winning streak and left a gaping hole in the roster. Joel Embiid missed the contest due to illness, and the team showed it cannot win without him. The residual star power on the roster failed to fill the void. This was not a close game where a single shot could have changed the outcome. It was a complete breakdown against a Western Conference opponent that exposed deep flaws in the lineup. Shooting Woes and Bench Gaps While Philadelphia converted just nine of 33 attempts, Portland sank 19 out of 42 three-pointers. That ten-made difference translated directly into 30 extra points for the Blazers, a margin that proved impossible to close. The game slipped away, Nick Nurse explained, as he pointed directly at the shooting numbers. “The big thing was the 3-point shooting,” Nurse said, according to Yahoo Sports . “It’s hard to lose by 10 on that particular stat. 10 makes. That’s 30 points. That’s hard to overcome.” A chilly 27 percent from range is a standout figure in any defeat, yet it stings more following a season beginning with high heat. The bench also failed to provide a spark. Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson combined for 35 of the 54 points scored by Portland’s reserves. By comparison, the Sixers bench produced a mere 24 points in total. Before foul trouble derailed his night, Jaylen Brown resembled his former self in the first half, scoring 19 points on 8-for-10 shooting. “I wasn’t too happy about it,” Brown said. “It’s over with now. I think that affected the game. It also affected my rhythm a little bit in the second half.” Arenas Warns of Future Matchups Western Conference foes especially worry Gilbert Arenas regarding future issues for the Philadelphia 76ers. Following the home defeat inflicted on Philadelphia by the Portland Trail Blazers, the ex-NBA icon voiced his worries on “Gil’s Arena”. He began his assessment with Philadelphia’s lineup. “Players seem like they’re still trying to figure out what is expected of them because their roles are changing every other game. You have no consistency in this lineup,” he said, according to AOL.com . That three-time All-Star also pinpointed the specific matchups likely to trouble the Sixers: “Their problem is going to be guards that can shoot and drive; they’re going to have a problem with that. … It’s just going to be certain matchups. It’s not going to be in their favor, right?” Arenas noted that the West is very heavy and fast-paced, while the East often tries to grind games out. He warned that if a team is not built to run, it will be run out of the building. After a tight first half, Portland surged ahead and almost hit the 130-point threshold. Tied at 69-69 when halftime arrived, the Blazers defeated Philadelphia 59-42 during the last two quarters. Lacking Embiid and with Brown restricted, the squad could not counter Portland’s shooting volume or size.

item.title: NASCAR Finally Fixes The Double-Line Rule For 2027
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR is finally shaking up the 2027 season with bold moves that fans have demanded for years. For the 2027 Daytona 500, Jimmie Johnson will drive the iconic No. 48 car, a major surprise originating from Hendrick Motorsports. This marks a historic moment as Johnson prepares for his final start in the Cup Series. Alex Bowman, who has driven the number since 2021, will give up the ride for this specific race but remains with the team for the full season. Johnson Returns to His Legacy Car While piloting the No. 48 Chevrolet, Johnson secured seven championships and 83 Cup Series races, according to a report . He has not raced full-time since 2020, making this return a rare treat for the sport. Reflecting on the memories and relationships connected to the No. 48, the seven-time champion stated that returning to it was “far more than a number,.” Bowman will still compete at Daytona, though the team has not yet confirmed which temporary number he will use. Due to its history within the team, the No. 25 has appeared as a potential alternative. New Rules Aim to Fix Boring Races Beyond the car number drama, NASCAR is overhauling rules to make racing more exciting. From the May race at Charlotte Motor Speedway onward, the sanctioning body will raise horsepower from 670 to 750. Superspeedway time trials are also cut from two rounds to one to save time and add drama. Autoweek reports that NASCAR also updated the controversial “double-line” rule to clarify when a driver is beneath the line. The new rule states a driver is considered beneath the double-line “when the vehicle’s left-side tires are beneath the left line of the inside double painted lines that separate the apron from the racing surface.” Kansas Speedway Adds IndyCar to the Mix Modifications also affect the track schedule, notably as Kansas Speedway hosts IndyCar again after 17 years. The track will host a four-series weekend in May 2027, featuring IndyCar, NASCAR Cup, Truck, and ARCA races. According to Kansas Speedway president Pat Warren, this addition provides fans with extra racing action over a single weekend. Highlighting the series’ growing momentum and the track’s history of tight competition, IndyCar president Doug Boles also embraced the return. The ARCA Menards Series starts the Kansas Speedway weekend on Friday, May 7, while the NASCAR Cup Series concludes the event on Sunday, May 9.

item.title: Chiefs React to NFL’s Announcement Involving Rookie Emmett Johnson
item.description: Emmett Johnson has been one of the best rookies in the NFL this season. He continued to impress last Sunday during the Kansas City Chiefs’ 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The team reacted to the league’s announcement involving the running back. He led the backfield with 23 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown, stepping up again in Kenneth Walker III’s absence. Johnson also showed his prowess as a receiver with four receptions for 38 yards. The 23-year-old was the 161st overall pick in the fifth round this year. He has outplayed his draft status and proving that he belongs in the NFL. It won’t be surprising if Johnson earns major awards after the season if he continues to play at a high level. Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson (10) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Arrowhead Stadium. Chiefs Comments on Emmett Johnson NFL Development The NFL announced that Emmett Johnson is one of the nominees for the Week 11 Rookie of the Week. Joining him are Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams and kicker Drew Stevens. Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman rounds out the list. “Who should be the @pepsi Rookie of the Week for Week 11? Vote in the poll below. ,” the league wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) Kansas City dropped its reaction in the comments section. “Chiefs Kingdom… you know what to do!! Give @emmettj_ some love ,” the Chiefs commented. Johnson already has 71 rushing attempts for 317 yards and two touchdowns this year. He also has 24 receptions for 345 yards and three more scores under his name, making a strong case for the Rookie of the Year award. He and Kansas City will play their next game on Thursday against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. The highly-anticipated Thanksgiving night showdown will be the first of their three-game road trip. The Chiefs are 8-2 for the season, while the Bills are tied for the NFL’s best record at 9-1. The team reacted to the league’s announcement involving the running back. He led the backfield with 23 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown, stepping up again in Kenneth Walker III’s absence. Johnson also showed his prowess as a receiver with four receptions for 38 yards. The 23-year-old was the 161st overall pick in the fifth round this year. He has outplayed his draft status and proving that he belongs in the NFL. It won’t be surprising if Johnson earns major awards after the season if he continues to play at a high level. Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson (10) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Arrowhead Stadium. Chiefs Comments on Emmett Johnson NFL Development The NFL announced that Emmett Johnson is one of the nominees for the Week 11 Rookie of the Week. Joining him are Washington Commanders wide receiver Antonio Williams and kicker Drew Stevens. Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman rounds out the list. “Who should be the @pepsi Rookie of the Week for Week 11? Vote in the poll below. ,” the league wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) Kansas City dropped its reaction in the comments section. “Chiefs Kingdom… you know what to do!! Give @emmettj_ some love ,” the Chiefs commented. Johnson already has 71 rushing attempts for 317 yards and two touchdowns this year. He also has 24 receptions for 345 yards and three more scores under his name, making a strong case for the Rookie of the Year award. He and Kansas City will play their next game on Thursday against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. The highly-anticipated Thanksgiving night showdown will be the first of their three-game road trip. item.title: CBS reporter shares how Colston Loveland reacted to being carted off during Lions-Bears
item.description: Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images Colston Loveland was carted off inside the first quarter of the Chicago Bears’ Thanksgiving Day game against the Detroit Lions. The tight end was ruled out of the game with a knee injury, with the 22-year-old suffering the injury in what seemed a fairly innocuous incident involving a Lions defender. The Bears are already without tight ends Cole Kmet and Hayden Large. Not only are the eyes of America watching the matchup at Ford Field, but the game is also massive in terms of the NFC North. The injury sustained by Loveland was clearly a lot for him to take in, with one CBS reporter sharing his immediate reaction. Sideline reporter shares Colston Loveland’s reaction after suffering knee injury CBS’ Tracy Wolfson was standing on the sideline to catch Loveland’s reaction, with the tight end left visually upset as he was carted away into the Bears’ locker room. “Jim, just an update on tight end Colston Loveland: we saw him being carted off the field. He was in tears, he was frustrated, and he is officially out with a knee injury. Rookie Sam Roush is now tight end number one for the Bears,” she said. Although no further update has been shared on the extent of Loveland’s injury, it has to be said that his emotional reaction may not be a great indication for Bears fans. Loveland has scored three touchdowns this season, but he offers a whole lot more, with the tight end blocking for a D’Andre Swift run when he suffered the injury. Ben Johnson’s offense has been incredibly diverse this season, but losing yet another tight end to injury is going to limit his options. The Seattle Seahawks were unable to deal with the Bears’ offense, but with significant players missing, weaknesses could be seen as the season pans out. item.title: Juventus keeping close tabs on 19-year-old Real Madrid attacking prodigy – report
item.description: Juventus keeping close tabs on 19-year-old Real Madrid attacking prodigy – report The Real Madrid academy has been home to several top talents in the recent past, as the club have been extremely successful in nurturing these players. And despite many departures in the recent past, the academy has continued to produce top talents. One of them is Daniel Yanez, an explosive winger currently plying his trade for Castilla. Yanez is regarded as one of the most promising young talents at Castilla right now and was linked with a potential move away from Valdebebas earlier in the summer. Juventus keeping close tabs Although Yanez ended up staying at Castilla, his future is far from certain as top teams continue to monitor his progress. According to Calciomercato , Juventus are among the clubs keeping tabs on Yanez as they look to prise him away from Valdebebas in the near future. Yanez has featured for Real Madrid first team only thrice. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The report adds that Juventus sporting director Marco Ottolini was in Spain this week to attend the UEFA Youth League match between Real Madrid U19 and PSV Eindhoven at the Alfredo Di Stefano Stadium. Ottolini attended the game specifically to watch Yanez in action. And the youngster did not disappoint either, playing a starring role in a 3-3 draw, notably scoring a goal while mustering an assist as well. In doing so, Yanez also matched the record of Benfica’s Pedro Alvaro for the most appearances in the UEFA Youth League (28). What’s in store for Yanez at Real Madrid? As Juventus continue to monitor the progress of Yanez, it is hard to imagine the young winger remaining at Real Madrid for long. Yanez has a contract at Real Madrid until 2029. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Despite showing exceptional talent and potential, Yanez doesn’t have any prospect of making a breakthrough in the first team, where even players like Endrick and Brahim Diaz are struggling with a lack of game time. A move away from Real Madrid, therefore, would be the most logical outcome for the young Spaniard. The challenge for Real Madrid will be to convince Yanez to not leave permanently, and perhaps settle for a loan move to a top-tier club. Even if they do sell the forward, the club will be keen on holding onto the player’s transfer rights – a method they have used liberally in the last few years.

item.title: Wyndham Clark reveals what Jackson Koivun was really like in the Presidents Cup team room
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Jackson Koivun made his Presidents Cup debut at Medinah earlier this year. Wyndham Clark was also on the US team, so he got to see Koivun up close and personal throughout the week. The US team beat the International side 17-13 in the end, but the contest was actually a lot closer than that scoreline suggests throughout the Sunday singles. Jackson Koivun won his singles match against Si Woo Kim and that was a huge turning point in the outcome of the Presidents Cup . And now Wyndham Clark has opened up on what the young star was really like behind closed doors throughout the week in Illinois. Wyndham Clark reveals what Jackson Koivun was like at the Presidents Cup Clark got to know Koivun well during the Presidents Cup this year, having not spent much time with him previously. The two-time major champion made an appearance on The Vanity Index Podcast on Wednesday, and was asked what Koivun was like behind the scenes at Medinah. “ He was really impressive, “ Clark admitted. “ He fit into the team really well. You know, I think as a rookie, you kind of don’t know what to expect, and you’re kind of quiet at first, but then as the guys make you feel comfortable, which I think we did a good job of, he kind of came out of his shell and was fun. “ When we talked trash, he kind of started dishing it back, and then I think we saw his confidence grow with each match that he played, and then obviously at the end winning his match in the singles. “ So yeah, he was great, and I think he’ll be on a bunch of teams going forward. “ Koivun was one of the shining lights for the US team at the Presidents Cup this year. The experience he gained at Medinah will be crucial for him as he plays on more Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup teams in the future. The fact that Koivun went unbeaten throughout the week at Medinah tells us all we need to know about his quality, and Clark’s comments suggest that he is more than comfortable mixing with the biggest names in the game. The 21-year-old has absolutely everything needed to go to the very top of the sport, and it would be a huge shock if he wasn’t on the US Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor in 2027.

item.title: Alex Campos shares emotional message after Barcelona debut: ‘Days that you dream of living’
item.description: Alex Campos shares emotional message after Barcelona debut: ‘Days that you dream of living’ Wednesday night turned out be a memorable one for Barcelona starlet Alex Campos as he made his first-team debut in the UEFA Champions League clash against Sabah FK. The 18-year-old defensive starlet came on for the final 25 minutes of the game as the Catalans cruised to a 4-1 victory at the Baku Olympic Stadium in Azerbaijan. Alex Campos at a loss for words after debut Now, taking to social media, Campos has expressed his delight after making his first-team debut for Barcelona, describing the occasion as a childhood dream that left him struggling to find the right words. Posting pictures of his time on the field against Sabah, the teenage defender wrote: “There are days that you dream of living since childhood and when they arrive, it’s hard to find words to describe them. “Yesterday I had the privilege of fulfilling one of these dreams: debuting with the first team of FC Barcelona in the Champions League.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Alex Campos Cami (@aleexcampos_) The La Masia graduate also expressed his gratitude to the people who supported him throughout his journey into professional football. “Thanks to my family, teammates, coaches and all the people who have been part of this journey and helped me get here,” he wrote. Concluding, Campos made it clear that this was only the start as he wants to keep playing for the Blaugrana senior team. “Now we have to continue working to have more opportunities to live moments like this, always from humility and effort. Visca el Barça! “ An impressive first step Campos has been at La Masia since a young age and has enjoyed steady development through the ranks at the Barcelona youth setup. Alex Campos made his first-team debut vs Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) The 18-year-old starlet has become a regular presence for Juliano Belletti’s Barça Atletic team this season, while also featuring in several matchday squads for the first team under Hansi Flick owing to injuries. Indeed, Campos was called up by the German manager for six matches before he finally made his debut against Sabah. And, while it was a short cameo, the teenager did enough to leave a major impression . Campos displayed great maturity during his brief appearance, while also being composed and comfortable with the ball at his feet. With a busy period ahead for the senior team, the youngster could prove to be a genuine rotation option for Flick.

item.title: Joshua Zirkzee back on the radar of Premier League rivals as Man United consider changes in attack in January
item.description: Joshua Zirkzee back on the radar of Premier League rivals as Man United consider changes in attack in January Joshua Zirkzee earned a rare start for Manchester United when they took on Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday. The Dutchman impressed but could not find the back of the net and was eventually replaced in the 64th minute as the Red Devils had to settle for a point due to terrible refereeing and glaring mistakes from Senne Lammens . The former Bologna ace has accrued 295 minutes across all competitions this season and has two goals to his name. However, none of the previous United managers ever fully trusted the Netherlands international. Page 1 of 2 1 2 Which is why the 25-year-old remains keen to leave in search of regular minutes in January. Multiple Serie A clubs are reportedly monitoring the situation with interest. Everton back in for Joshua Zirkzee They are not the only ones eyeing the forward, with Everton also reportedly open to returning for his services once the transfer window reopens. The Toffees had launched a stunning deadline-day move for Joshua Zirkzee, but United rejected the approach as they could not bring in an alternative of their own. Sky Sports United No. 11 is on the list. “But Everton are approaching the next window looking to do two particular pieces of business, primarily a recognised striker to compete with Thierno Barry. Pochettino will have the final say “A renewed attempt for either Richarlison, Zirkzee or Balogun has not been ruled out.” Mauricio Pochettino will have the final say, and judging from his utilisation of the former Bayern Munich starlet, the Argentine likes his link-up abilities. But with Benjamin Sesko injured, and Bryan Mbeumo misfiring, the Red Devils need an all-out finisher and INEOS are expected to bring in one in January . In that case, given the meagre budget and the need to strengthen in defence, Joshua Zirkzee could be let go. Time will tell whether he can change the club’s mind.

item.title: Steelers Get Back Key Reinforcement vs. Broncos
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. during a preseason game against the Green Bay Packers on Aug. 13, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers have activated wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (left foot) off injured reserve. He also has no injury designation for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos after practicing in all three practicies this week. Pittman was placed on injured reserve with a left foot injury on Saturday, Oct. 10. “I’m very confident that Michael Pittman should be out there this week,” Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday. Pittman was a full participant last Thursday and Friday’s practice, after being limited on Wednesday while trying to return to action. Pittman 21-day practice window opened last Wednesday. Pittman said last Wednesday that he wants to make sure he’s effective when he’s back out there. If he’s feeling good, he believes he can make a difference by “just being out there when I’m needed,” Pittman said. “Just those opportunities out there, just creating plays, throw some nice blocks and just play hard. Just bring that physicality and just someone that the guys can depend on. And just be there for any situation. If it’s a ‘run the ball’ type game, hey, I’m in there to block safeties and linebackers.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps is a mess right now . DK Metcalf hasn’t lived up to his lucrative contract, and injuries have been a big issue for receivers like Pittman and Roman Wilson . Wilson returned on Sunday after missing four games due to a left hand injury. Perhaps with Pittman and Wilson back in the fold it can provide a boost for the Steelers’ stagnant offense. The Steelers also have a quartrerback change with Mason Rudolph inserted into the starting lineup after the abrupt benching and release of Aaron Rodgers . item.title: NBA Thanksgiving: 10 Reasons to Give Thanks in 2026, Including a Legendary NY Knicks Title Run
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This has been a wild year in the NBA. The New York Knicks took fans on a legendary ride to their first NBA championship in over 50 years. Victor Wembanyama staked his claim as the new face of the league. LeBron James changed teams, again, and for a discount rate. And some from the 2026 crop of NBA Draft picks are already making an impact. On this Thanksgiving Day, we look at what we are giving thanks for from the NBA in 2026. Detroit Pistons are here to stay Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives past Los Angeles Lakers guard Matisse Thybulle (4) in the first half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The Detroit Pistons have a devoted fanbase and rich history. However, during the 2020s, their supporters have endured some awful seasons. However, two years ago, they showed life by finishing above .500 for the first time in a decade. Then they took a big step forward, finishing with the best record in the Eastern Conference last season. In 2026-27, they are a legitimate NBA Finals contender. There is no doubt, the Pistons are back and here to stay with a young core that should keep them competitive for the foreseeable future. The NBA is always better when there is a strong team playing in Motown. We give thanks for that. Stephen Curry will finish career with Golden State Warriors Nov 9, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) reacts after scoring a three point basket against the New Orleans Pelicans during the third quarter at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images This summer, as the Golden State Warriors failed to make a meaningful addition, speculation spread that Stephen Curry may be unhappy and choose not to finish his career with the franchise. There were even some who thought he might go to the Charlotte Hornets because of the family ties to the organization. However, before the new season started, Curry inked a new multi-year deal that should mean he spends his entire Hall of Fame career with one team. With stars always moving around in sports, it is always good to see a legend stick with just one team. Los Angeles Clippers blasted with penalties for cap circumvention Oct 10, 2023; Seattle, Washington, USA; LA Clippers owner Steve Balmer ends a speech before the first quarter against the Utah Jazz at Climate Pledge Arena. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-USA TODAY Sports When the news broke last year that the Los Angeles Clippers created shell companies to win the free agent chase for Kawhi Leonard in 2019 and pay him extra money outside of the salary cap, it enraged fans. They hoped for a stiff penalty but had doubts the NBA would actually go through with it. Well, they did, in a huge way. The Clippers got hit with a $30 million fine, the owner was banned for a year, and losing five future first-round picks were among the punishments. LA messed around, and they found o

Victor Wembanyama staked his claim as the new face of the league. LeBron James changed teams, again, and for a discount rate. And some from the 2026 crop of NBA Draft picks are already making an impact. On this Thanksgiving Day, we look at what we are giving thanks for from the NBA in 2026. Detroit Pistons are here to stay Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives past Los Angeles Lakers guard Matisse Thybulle (4) in the first half at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The Detroit Pistons have a devoted fanbase and rich history. However, during the 2020s, their supporters have endured some awful seasons. However, two years ago, they showed life by finishing above .500 for the first time in a decade. Then they took a big step forward, finishing with the best record in the Eastern Conference last season. In 2026-27, they are a legitimate NBA Finals contender. There is no doubt, the Pistons are back and here to stay with a young core that should keep them competitive for the foreseeable future. The NBA is always better when there is a strong team playing in Motown. We give thanks for that. Stephen Curry will finish career with Golden State Warriors Nov 9, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) reacts after scoring a three point basket against the New Orleans Pelicans during the third quarter at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images This summer, as the Golden State Warriors failed to make a meaningful addition, speculation spread that Stephen Curry may be unhappy and choose not to finish his career with the franchise. There were even some who thought he might go to the Charlotte Hornets because of the family ties to the organization. However, before the new season started, Curry inked a new multi-year deal that should mean he spends his entire Hall of Fame career with one team. With stars always moving around in sports, it is always good to see a legend stick with just one team. Los Angeles Clippers blasted with penalties for cap circumvention Oct 10, 2023; Seattle, Washington, USA; LA Clippers owner Steve Balmer ends a speech before the first quarter against the Utah Jazz at Climate Pledge Arena. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-USA TODAY Sports When the news broke last year that the Los Angeles Clippers created shell companies to win the free agent chase for Kawhi Leonard in 2019 and pay him extra money outside of the salary cap, it enraged fans. They hoped for a stiff penalty but had doubts the NBA would actually go through with it. Well, they did, in a huge way. The Clippers got hit with a $30 million fine, the owner was banned for a year, and losing five future first-round picks were among the punishments. LA messed around, and they found out big time you don’t circumvent the salary cap to sign players. New York Knicks became America’s team Jun 18, 2026; New York, NY, USA; Teammates cheer as New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson is called up to receive a key to the city from mayor Zohran Mamdani during a ceremony at New York City Hall after the championship parade. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images New York sports fans are used to their counterparts from other cities hating their teams because of where they come from. However, the Knicks did something special this spring. By way of one of the most entertaining playoff runs in history, they actually made fans around the country root for a New York team to win a championship. The Knicks’ players and style of play were so captivating that there were even some NBA pundits who called them the new “America’s team.” Whether you were rooting for them or not, the NBA was as good as ever in the spring because of Knickerbockers and we give thanks for that. LeBron James makes the Philadelphia 76ers must-see TV Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) controls the ball against the Chicago Bulls during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images After getting their doors blown off by the Knicks in the semifinals, the Philadelphia 76ers knew they had to make some big changes. But most doubted they would be able to. However, they somehow got the Boston Celtics to trade them Jaylen Brown , which then convinced LeBron James to surprisingly come to Philly at a discount rate. Brown going to the Sixers is a big deal. But James joining them makes Philadelphia one of the most fascinating teams in the NBA. They are a rare super-team in a luxury tax era. They will be a fun talking point for fans in and outside of Philadelphia all season, and we give thanks for that. Victor Wembanyama begins rise to being the new face of the NBA Nov 9, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) against the Phoenix Suns in the second half at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images There was a massive amount of hype surrounding the French phenom when he entered the league three years ago. He showed great potential in his rookie season and was primed to make a big jump in the 2024-25 season. Unfortunately, a blood clot halted his ascension. Well, that only motivated Wembanyama. Last season, he became the dominant force scouts predicted and turned the San Antonio Spurs into one of the elite teams in the league. In the spring, while the Knicks were having a magical run, the Spurs were having an equally impressive showing with their young core led by Wembanyama, as they rampaged through the postseason and ousted the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder . We needed the next top star after James, and NBA fans now have it in Wembanyama. Milwaukee Bucks finally traded Giannis Antetokounmpo Nov 10, 2026; Salt Lake City, Utah, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) flexes after dunking the basketball during the second half against the Utah Jazz at Delta Center. Mandatory Credit: Chris Nicoll-Imagn Images The saga of whether the Milwaukee Bucks would trade Giannis Antetokounmpo became like a soap opera as neither side wanted to end the relationship. However, after an awful campaign last season, they finally pulled the trigger on a trade to the Miami Heat . The trade chase lasted for months and was equal parts fascinating and annoying. We give thanks for it finally being over. The end of tanking? Jun 23, 2026; New York, NY, USA; NBA commissioner Adam Silver poses for a photo with the draft prospects before the start of the 2026 NBA Draft at Barclays Center. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The idea of tanking was forever changed in the NBA this year. Teams like the Utah Jazz , Brooklyn Nets , and Clippers blatantly began to tank early in the season and purposefully sit impact talent, and the league and its fans had enough. So the NBA changed the guidelines for how many ping-pong balls teams with the worst records get in the lottery. The goal is to hopefully force clubs to stay competitive to the end of the year for their fans. Who knows if it will work, but the league seeing a big problem and trying to fix it was a good thing. Portland Trail Blazers are actually for real Nov 11, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Portland Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija (8) reacts after dunking the ball against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images The Portland Trail Blazers roster has had to deal with a lot of nonsense over the last year. To begin last season, their head coach, Chauncey Billups, was arrested for his links to a poker scheme. They got a new owner who they fast found out is a bit of a cheapskate. Then the coach who led them through the drama to the playoffs for the first time since 2021, Thiago

item.title: 'I have no regrets': Mohammed Shami opens up on Test retirement, says he's happy with what he received
item.description: MUMBAI: Mohammed Shami didn't have a particularly fruitful outing in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy, finishing with four wickets in seven matches@43.00, at an economy rate of 8.60. On Thursday, he conceded 0-19 in three overs, as Bengal lost their must-win final league match to Rajasthan by six wickets to crash out of the tournament. However, the veteran pacer, who announced his Test retirement about a month back, has moved beyond purely worrying about his own performances. Shami was pleased to see the emergence of some young talent in the BCCI’s domestic tournament. "Overall, it was a good outing, because I got to see a lot of things, a few youngsters in our team. I got to see some new talent as well. And I hope that from this tournament, we will get to see new faces in the auctions. I am getting to see good talent and skill. Hopefully, some new guys emerge from this season," Shami told reporters at the Wankhede Stadium on Thursday. The 36-year-old fast bowler may have hung his boots in Test cricket, but he has no plans of slowing down. The veteran India fast bowler is keen to continue playing white-ball cricket, and in the Ranji Trophy for Bengal. For Shami, the motivation to keep playing still remains the same as before. “I have said this before: I will continue playing white-ball cricket, and if required, I will play red-ball cricket as well for (maintaining my) fitness. I’ve been doing this for the last 15-20 years. It’s the same old routine. Nothing new,” he said. Despite getting a raw deal from the national selectors for the past couple of years, Shami has no regrets about how his Test journey ended, after he enjoyed considerable success in the format, taking 229 wickets in 64 Tests@27.71, with six fivers, between 2012-2023. It was only last season when Shami showcased what magic he can conjure up with the red ball, taking eight for 90 against Jammu & Kashmir in the Ranji Trophy semifinal. However, nine months later, the ace pacer announced his Test retirement. Rated as one of India’s best fast bowlers ever, Shami has now learnt to brush off any disappointment or regret and has made peace with what life has given him. “I have no regrets. Whatever I got was what was destined for me. You get only what the Almighty has written in your destiny. I am happy with whatever I have received. Now, I will play as much as I am destined to and enjoy it,” he said. The fast bowler is also keen to keep playing for Bengal in domestic cricket, where he believes his experience can be valuable to younger players. Shami sees this as an opportunity to give something back. “There’s no question of losing motivation. As long as you love cricket and enjoy playing the game, you should continue. I have said this before as well. As long as you are enjoying it, you should keep playing. That is my motivation. Also, if we can help a few youngsters in some way, that would be even better. item.content:encoded: MUMBAI: Mohammed Shami didn't have a particularly fruitful outing in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy, finishing with four wickets in seven matches@43.00, at an economy rate of 8.60. On Thursday, he conceded 0-19 in three overs, as Bengal lost their must-win final league match to Rajasthan by six wickets to crash out of the tournament. However, the veteran pacer, who announced his Test retirement about a month back, has moved beyond purely worrying about his own performances. Shami was pleased to see the emergence of some young talent in the BCCI’s domestic tournament. "Overall, it was a good outing, because I got to see a lot of things, a few youngsters in our team. I got to see some new talent as well. And I hope that from this tournament, we will get to see new faces in the auctions. I am getting to see good talent and skill. Hopefully, some new guys emerge from this season," Shami told reporters at the Wankhede Stadium on Thursday. The 36-year-old fast bowler may have hung his boots in Test cricket, but he has no plans of slowing down. For Shami, the motivation to keep playing still remains the same as before. “I have said this before: I will continue playing white-ball cricket, and if required, I will play red-ball cricket as well for (maintaining my) fitness. I’ve been doing this for the last 15-20 years. It’s the same old routine. Nothing new,” he said. Despite getting a raw deal from the national selectors for the past couple of years, Shami has no regrets about how his Test journey ended, after he enjoyed considerable success in the format, taking 229 wickets in 64 Tests@27.71, with six fivers, between 2012-2023. It was only last season when Shami showcased what magic he can conjure up with the red ball, taking eight for 90 against Jammu & Kashmir in the Ranji Trophy semifinal. However, nine months later, the ace pacer announced his Test retirement. Rated as one of India’s best fast bowlers ever, Shami has now learnt to brush off any disappointment or regret and has made peace with what life has given him. “I have no regrets. Whatever I got was what was destined for me. You get only what the Almighty has written in your destiny. I am happy with whatever I have received. Now, I will play as much as I am destined to and enjoy it,” he said. The fast bowler is also keen to keep playing for Bengal in domestic cricket, where he believes his experience can be valuable to younger players. Shami sees this as an opportunity to give something back. “There’s no question of losing motivation. As long as you love cricket and enjoy playing the game, you should continue. I have said this before as well. As long as you are enjoying it, you should keep playing. That is my motivation. Also, if we can help a few youngsters in some way, that would be even better. Especially when you play for your state, experience matters a lot,” he said. Will he play in the Vijay Hazare Trophy too? “Sure,” pat came the reply, before Shami outlined that he now had the option to “pick and choose” his matches. “I have the option of picking and choosing. I can decide which matches I want to play and which ones I don’t. There is no pressure. Hopefully, I’m fit for the season ahead and things keep going well,” he said. While a return to international white-ball cricket remains a possibility, Shami is not spending his time thinking about the next World Cup cycle. The 2027 ODI World Cup and the 2028 T20 World Cup may be on the horizon, but Shami would rather concentrate on what is immediately in front of him. “I have stopped thinking about all these things. Right now, my focus is on my game. Whatever decision they (the national selectors) take will be better. I just want to focus on staying fit, keep playing for my state (Bengal) and enjoy the sport,” Shami asserted. ‘Avoid early starts in SMAT’ Shami concurred with former India players Irfan Pathan and Wasim Jaffer that 9am, or 8am starts in case of Kolkata, where Mumbai are playing their league matches, are too early for SMAT games. "I have also said this before, that the T20 format (games) should start at around 12-1pm. If you are playing two matches everyday, then those games should be held in the afternoon and evening. Because in the morning, there is a lot of dew and moisture in the wicket this season. So, I think the toss becomes a (big) factor somewhere," Shami felt. Backs call for using saliva on the ball During the 2025 Champions Trophy in Dubai, Shami had appealed to the cricket authorities to revoke the ban on saliva in order to allow pace bowlers to rediscover swing and reverse swing. It wasn't surprising, therefore, that Shami backed India captain Shubman Gill’s suggestion after India's drawn test against New Zealand at Wellington that bowlers should be allowed to apply saliva on the ball since covid was long gone. “I back Shubman’s statement on allowing bowlers to apply saliva on the ball. Kuchh toh maza aye red ball mein... (Red-ball cricket should have some added fun!),” Shami said.

item.title: UTSA vs. Tulsa football: Preview, scouting report, betting info and prediction
item.description: UTSA Roadrunner head coach Jeff Traylor reacts after a touchdown during the second quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Sizing up the American Conference championship race last week, UTSA coach Jeff Traylor at least figured the schedule would be on his side. The Roadrunners were part of a three-way deadlock alongside Memphis and North Texas for the top spot in the league standings with two games remaining, and any tiebreaker between them would likely come down to computer rankings. With a pair of strong remaining opponents in UAB and Tulsa, Traylor knew UTSA had a chance to make up ground in the metrics. But with Memphis and North Texas both losing early Saturday and UTSA securing a 19-17 win against UAB that night, the Roadrunners have a chance to render tiebreakers and analytics irrelevant. A win against Tulsa at 11 a.m. Friday in the Alamodome assures UTSA a first-place finish in the American Conference, giving the Roadrunners the right to host next week's championship game. "If you would've told me that we would be in this position Week 1, I would tell you you're probably dreaming," UTSA offensive lineman Ben Rios said. "I can't believe we control our own destiny. But again, as coaches told us, we cannot look over this game. We're playing Tulsa, and we need to focus on Tulsa." READ MORE: How UTSA's recharged culture fuels championship contention beyond the stats UTSA is the first American Conference team to take the field this week, and the Roadrunners still have a path to the title game even with a loss to Tulsa, which would slip them into the pack of two-loss teams along with Memphis, East Carolina and North Texas. UTSA would host the championship if Memphis and ECU both lose this weekend, and the Roadrunners would also earn a berth with a North Texas loss and a loss by either Memphis or East Carolina. Any three- or four-way tie of two-loss teams becomes messy to untangle, as the league would rely on a composite of four computer rankings. While UTSA struggles in the predictive SP+ efficiency metric the conference utilizes, the Roadrunners rate well in the league's other three measures that focus on resume and strength of record: SportSource TR116 TSR, ESPN SOR and KPI. Of course, the tiebreakers are only relevant if UTSA loses to Tulsa, and a loss to Tulsa could significantly diminish UTSA's standing in the metrics. The cleanest path to the Roadrunners' seasonlong goal of claiming a conference title remains winning Friday's game. "Of course, we've talked about it," linebacker Cam Cooper said, "but we've got to go take care of Tulsa first." UTSA Roadrunners running back Will Henderson III runs the ball toward the end zone in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. "Of course, we've talked about it," linebacker Cam Cooper said, "but we've got to go take care of Tulsa first." UTSA Roadrunners running back Will Henderson III runs the ball toward the end zone in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Tulsa (7-4, 4-3 American Conference) at UTSA (9-2, 6-1) When: 11 a.m. Friday Where: Alamodome, San Antonio TV: ESPN Radio: 760 AM All-time series: Tied 1-1 Last meeting: Tulsa 46, UTSA 45 on Oct. 26, 2024, in Tulsa, Okla. Tulsa at UTSA betting info Spread: UTSA –1.5 Over/under: 57.5 What to know about Tulsa Last game: Tulsa 42, Charlotte 14 on Nov. 21 in Tulsa Players to watch: Traylor dubbed Tulsa quarterback Baylor Hayes with the nickname "Baller Baylor" this week, highlighting his athleticism, timing and ability to escape pressure. He's averaged 310.7 passing yards per game during Tulsa's three-game winning streak, notching 20 touchdowns and four interceptions for the year. "He's out there having fun, man. I can't wait to go against him," Cooper said. "It's an honor to go against him." UTSA vs. Tulsa: 5 players to watch as Roadrunners look to secure home field When UTSA has the ball Twitchy defensive ends Kyran Duhon (8 sacks) and Thomas Davis (7 sacks) will test UTSA's offensive line. "They honestly are a lot better than their record shows," Rios said. "We're going to have to step up this game, for sure." The status of running back A'Marion Peterson will also be a factor for the Roadrunners, as the program's single-season touchdown record holder with 17 this year. He did not play in last week's second half due to an apparent lower-body injury. When Tulsa has the ball Traylor said Tulsa is "the team in our league right now that's playing the best football," riding a streak of five straight games scoring at least 35 points. But UTSA's defense is on its best run of the season, too, giving up just 304 yards in a 35-16 win against North Texas and then yielding only 227 yards in a 19-17 win over UAB. Key matchup UTSA vs. External factors If the championship stakes weren't enough, the Roadrunners are also facing the emotions of senior day, a whirlwind of noise around Traylor's candidacy for jobs at Baylor and TCU, and a rare 11 a.m. kickoff on a short week. When UTSA last played a home game at 11 a.m., Colorado State returned the opening kickoff for a touchdown on the way to a 14-0 lead less than two minutes into the game. "We're going to try to get off to a better start. It's going to be that way," Traylor said. "Families, tickets, tears. Been with these guys a long time. So, it'll be all that, but we got to hang in there early, and once we calm down, hope we can weather the storm." Prediction UTSA 32, Tulsa 28 As unpredictable as the Roadrunners' season has been, UTSA's home success has been as reliable as ever. Traylor is 28-1 against conference opponents in the Alamodome, and the Roadrunners aren't likely to let that streak end in a matchup with so much on the line. item.title: 4 Reasons Why MJF Will Lose to Will Ospreay at AEW Worlds End
item.description: AEW MJF’s pursuit of the AEW World Championship could hit a roadblock at Worlds End. The 30-year-old returned at Full Gear after Will Ospreay successfully defended his title against Kyle Fletcher in a hard-fought battle. MJF attacked the AEW World Champion with his custom championship belt, the Triple B, before escaping through the crowd. He showed up on the latest episode of Dynamite to challenge Ospreay to a title vs. title match at Worlds End on December 19. Although Ospreay was absent from the show because he had not been medically cleared to travel since AEW Full Gear, he accepted the challenge via a video message but added a major stipulation. The two will compete in a ladder match, with both championships hanging above the ring. While anything can happen on any given night, here are four major reasons why Will Ospreay might retain the gold at Worlds End. Ladder Match Could Favor Will Ospreay Ospreay is one of the most athletic performers in professional wrestling, and the ladder match stipulation could play right into his hands. His speed, agility, and ability to take risks could give him a significant advantage over his opponent. While Ospreay is comfortable using the ropes and creating opportunities with his high-flying moves, Maxwell Jacob Friedman often relies on slowing down his opponents and finding openings to exploit. MJF is well aware of this, which is why he was furious when the stipulation was added. MJF Has Been Out of Action for a While MJF’s last in-ring appearance was at All In London on August 30, where he competed in the Casino Gauntlet match, which Andrade El Idolo won. If he does not wrestle before Worlds End, MJF will step into the ring for a match after more than three months. His ring rust could give the champion even more of an advantage. The former AEW International Champion returned to AEW television at Full Gear, confronting Ospreay after the latter’s successful championship defense. It was his first appearance in over two months, as he had been away due to a combination of physical recovery and acting commitments outside professional wrestling. Will Ospreay Is Currently on an Incredible Run Will Ospreay defeated Kenny Omega at All In London to become the new AEW World Champion and has since established himself as one of the company’s top performers. The Aerial Assassin has delivered several impressive performances since winning the gold. In his nearly three months as champion, Ospreay has already defended the title four times. While he emerged victorious over Jon Moxley, Kazuchika Okada, and Kyle Fletcher in singles matches, the 33-year-old also retained the strap in an eight-man Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. MJF will have to find a way to get past a champion who has recently defeated some of the biggest names in the company. item.title: P.J. Washington Proves He Is The Mavs’ Secret Weapon
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Forget the old talk about needing a perfect third star. P.J. Washington is already doing the heavy lifting beside Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. He is the glue holding this Dallas roster together while everyone else chases headlines. Washington is the team’s third-leading scorer with 14.0 points per game through the first 18 contests. He also leads the Mavericks in rebounds at 6.6 per contest. This comes after he missed two games with an illness and still delivered a massive impact in Tuesday’s win. He posted 14 points, six rebounds, two steals, and one block against the Nuggets. He did not start the game, yet he finished with the highest plus-minus rating at 32. Aggression And Mismatches Washington knows how to use his size to hurt opponents. “I just tried to be aggressive,” Washington said. He felt like he found mismatches all over the floor and used his abilities to get downhill. He made easy shots and brought energy on the defensive end. His career-high 6.1 attempts per game from beyond the arc show his range, even if he only made one of three on Tuesday. The coaching staff trusts him in any spot. Dusty May said the team has many players who could start, so the starting lineup doesn’t matter. May felt the team found a defensive rhythm to begin games recently, so they just didn’t want to rock the boat. Washington excelled within the second unit, generating more offense while handling the ball somewhat more frequently. His defensive intensity was great, according to Dallas News. The Engine Behind The Win Cooper Flagg recognized Washington’s impact immediately during their joint postgame news conference. “I also wanted to shout out to P.J.,” Flagg said. The young star noted that Washington brought huge energy throughout the game alongside Naji Marshall and Morez Johnson Jr. Those guys are the defensive motors for Dallas. Denver was restricted to 40 percent shooting by the Mavericks, who capitalized on 18 turnovers to score 26 points. Jamal Murray, Nikola Jokic’s sidekick, finished with 20 points while Jokic himself was limited to just 18. Both fell below their season averages. The team is now on a four-game win streak and sits in the driver’s seat to win their NBA Cup group. If Houston defeats Phoenix on Wednesday, the Mavericks can secure a knockout round berth immediately. Up next for the Mavericks is a trip to Phoenix on Friday to finish group play.
item.content:encoded: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Forget the old talk about needing a perfect third star. P.J. Washington is already doing the heavy lifting beside Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. He is the glue holding this Dallas roster together while everyone else chases headlines. Washington is the team’s third-leading scorer with 14.0 points per game through the first 18 contests. He also leads the Mavericks in rebounds at 6.6 per contest. This comes after he missed two games with an illness and still delivered a massive impact in Tuesday’s win. He posted 14 points, six rebounds, two steals, and one block against the Nuggets. He did not start the game, yet he finished with the highest plus-minus rating at 32. Aggression And Mismatches Washington knows how to use his size to hurt opponents. “I just tried to be aggressive,” Washington said. He felt like he found mismatches all over the floor and used his abilities to get downhill. He made easy shots and brought energy on the defensive end. His career-high 6.1 attempts per game from beyond the arc show his range, even if he only made one of three on Tuesday. The coaching staff trusts him in any spot.
