item.title: Steelers owner Art Rooney II backs Mike McCarthy by calling out bad teammate Aaron Rodgers for ‘insubordination’
item.description: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Image Steelers owner Art Rooney II backs Mike McCarthy by calling out bad teammate Aaron Rodgers for ‘insubordination’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Earlier this week, Aaron Rodgers pulled off one of the more memorable PR stunts in recent sports history by going on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show and absolutely berating Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy . The move came just hours after Rodgers was benched by the Steelers for their upcoming game, and resulted in his dismissal from the team. Now, Steelers owner Art Rooney has weighed in on the controversy. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that,” said Rooney, per Brooke Pryor of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rooney also called Rodgers insubordinate and said he was “not a good teammate” when discussing the team’s decision to release him. It became apparent very quickly after Rodgers took to the airwaves on Wednesday that there was no possible path forward between himself and the Steelers, as he accused McCarthy of, among other things, sleeping through team meetings and skipping walk-throughs. While some sources have corroborated these claims, it doesn’t appear to be enough to put McCarthy on the hot seat, despite the Steelers’ last two ugly losses. In any case, it will certainly be interesting to see what kind of energy the Steelers come out with on Friday afternoon when they host the Denver Broncos at 3:00 pm ET. item.title: LeBron James Breaks Triple-Double Record At 41 Years Old
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James recorded 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds to lead the Philadelphia 76ers past the Miami Heat in an NBA Cup matchup on Wednesday night. The 41-year-old star posted his best all-around game for the franchise while setting a new mark as the oldest player to ever achieve a triple-double in NBA history, according to the Associated Press. Tyrese Maxey added 30 points to help secure a 111-104 victory for the home team in Philadelphia. The Sixers entered the contest without Joel Embiid, yet they managed to stop a Miami squad that arrived riding a seven-game winning streak, per PhillyVoice . The Associated Press reports that James caught a pass from VJ Edgecombe slightly beyond midcourt and made a 35-foot basket. He ran back with his palms extended and licked his lips as the crowd chanted his name while the arena blasted a remix song to nearly 20,000 screaming fans. A Historic Night for the King James now has 126 career triple-doubles, a number that exceeds the combined total of Larry Bird, Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant, and Scottie Pippen, according to the Associated Press. He scored 14 straight points during the second quarter. “I had a couple of opportunities, and I was able to connect on them,” James said. “I kind of know when my hand is feeling pretty good, especially from the outside. See how long I can keep it going.” For the fourth straight game, he has scored no fewer than 20 points, extending his current scoring run. Heat coach Erik Spoelstra, who coached James during Miami’s back-to-back championships in 2012 and 2013, offered high praise before the tip-off. Ahead of the game, Spoelstra said of James, “Father Time always wins. But right now, he’s giving Father Time hell.” The Impact on the Eastern Conference With this win, the 76ers improved their record to 15-4, which stands as the best mark in the Eastern Conference, per the Associated Press. James chose to join Philadelphia rather than return to Miami largely because of Tyrese Maxey, according to PhillyVoice. Coach Nick Nurse noted the team’s offensive efficiency before the game started. James addressed his ability to step up when the team needs him most. “If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time,” James said, “I can still accomplish that.” He turns 42 on Dec. 30, yet his play on Wednesday showed no signs of slowing down against a tough opponent. The Sixers now sit atop the conference standings despite the absence of their star center. PhillyVoice noted that James sealed his 14-point stretch in the second quarter by draining a 35-foot pull-up. The game took place on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, in Philadelphia.

item.title: Can FSU football upset No. 20 Florida to secure bowl eligibility
item.description: Florida State football has its coach of the future in Glenn Schumann, but his era won't officially begin until after the Seminoles' season finale against rival No. 20 Florida , under the leadership of interim head coach Rick Stockstill. The Seminoles are a win away from reaching bowl eligibility, and to achieve that, it will require a first win over the Gators since 2023 to secure it. FSU lost its last game to North Carolina State 28-10, while Florida held off an upset bid from Vanderbilt, winning 34-27. Tallahassee Democrat FSU Athletics beat reporter Liam Rooney breaks down the matchup. Quick facts Matchup: Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) vs. Florida (7-4, 5-4 ACC) Kickoff: 3:30 p.m. Friday; Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee TV/radio: ABC / Seminole Sports Network Spread: FSU +6 Scouting report: What to know about Florida With the ball: The Gators will bring a talented rushing attack to Tallahassee, averaging 169.5 yards per game, anchored by star running back Jadan Baugh. While Florida's rushing attack is a threat, Aaron Philo has settled in under center after some up-and-down moments this season. The Gators throw for 226.1 yards per game, and Philo has tossed nine touchdowns to five interceptions, while rushing for 280 yards and six scores. Averaging 395.6 yards of total offense, the Seminoles will be stress-tested again by another offense capable of hitting explosive plays. Without the ball: Florida's defense hasn't been what it would have hoped this season, but there is still plenty of talent on the Gators to give FSU a few headaches. The unit allows 26.7 points per game and an average of 356.3 yards of total offense per game. Linebacker Myles Graham has recorded 86 tackles, 5.5 for loss and he's got 4.5 sacks this season, and he stands behind a star offensive lineman in Jayden Woods, who has seven sacks and 11 tackles for loss. Get to know the Gators Run the Baugh: The Seminoles are very familiar with Baugh, who torched the defense for 266 yards and two touchdowns in last season's meeting in Gainesville. He's 20 yards away from a second straight 1,000-yard rushing season, entering the game with 980 yards to his name and 16 rushing scores, the most in the SEC and top-5 in the nation. The FSU defense allows 171 rushing yards per game, which will give Baugh, who averages 89.6 yards per game, another chance at a potential big game. Don't get lost in the Woods: One of the most explosive defenders in the country, Woods has wrecked opposing offensive lines this season to the tune of 45 total tackles, 11 for loss, seven sacks, and he's forced a pair of fumbles. Tallahassee Democrat FSU Athletics beat reporter Liam Rooney breaks down the matchup. Quick facts Matchup: Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) vs. Florida (7-4, 5-4 ACC) Kickoff: 3:30 p.m. Friday; Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee TV/radio: ABC / Seminole Sports Network Spread: FSU +6 Scouting report: What to know about Florida With the ball: The Gators will bring a talented rushing attack to Tallahassee, averaging 169.5 yards per game, anchored by star running back Jadan Baugh. While Florida's rushing attack is a threat, Aaron Philo has settled in under center after some up-and-down moments this season. The Gators throw for 226.1 yards per game, and Philo has tossed nine touchdowns to five interceptions, while rushing for 280 yards and six scores. Averaging 395.6 yards of total offense, the Seminoles will be stress-tested again by another offense capable of hitting explosive plays. Without the ball: Florida's defense hasn't been what it would have hoped this season, but there is still plenty of talent on the Gators to give FSU a few headaches. The unit allows 26.7 points per game and an average of 356.3 yards of total offense per game. Linebacker Myles Graham has recorded 86 tackles, 5.5 for loss and he's got 4.5 sacks this season, and he stands behind a star offensive lineman in Jayden Woods, who has seven sacks and 11 tackles for loss. Get to know the Gators Run the Baugh: The Seminoles are very familiar with Baugh, who torched the defense for 266 yards and two touchdowns in last season's meeting in Gainesville. He's 20 yards away from a second straight 1,000-yard rushing season, entering the game with 980 yards to his name and 16 rushing scores, the most in the SEC and top-5 in the nation. The FSU defense allows 171 rushing yards per game, which will give Baugh, who averages 89.6 yards per game, another chance at a potential big game. Don't get lost in the Woods: One of the most explosive defenders in the country, Woods has wrecked opposing offensive lines this season to the tune of 45 total tackles, 11 for loss, seven sacks, and he's forced a pair of fumbles. With an FSU offensive line that has had some pass protection issues this season, Woods will be able to get pressure on Ashton Daniels under center, which will force him into making quick decisions. Liam Rooney's two cents Can the Seminoles move the ball?: FSU struggled to move the ball against North Carolina State, amassing one drive of 40-or-more yards, the opening drive of the game, which went 85 yards for a touchdown. Daniels struggled under center, and he wasn't able to consistently connect with his receivers while rushing for only 19 yards on 12 carries. That's not going to help the Seminoles win and secure bowl eligibility, so it will take a revitalized effort from the offense to pull off the upset over the Gators. Will FSU have any answer for the UF run game?: It's the defining question of the game, and if the answer is no, it will be another long night for the Seminoles. Baugh, alongside Philo and Duke Clark (57 carries, 358 yards, 3 touchdowns), will be a trio that gives FSU's defense maybe its toughest rushing test since the game agaisnt Miami. The Seminoles allowed NC State's Davion Gause to rack up 205 total yards of offense (134 rushing yards, 71 receiving yards), and if that level of defensive performance is replicated against the Gators, who average 4.3 yards per carry, the chances of a bowl game and an upset are slim. The pick The Seminoles have a new coach, and an interim in Stockstill, that has elevated the vibes around the program. While there may be a hopeful future ahead of the university, Florida's strengths will exploit the areas where FSU struggles. Baugh has not rushed for more than 100 yards in a game since a September loss to Ole Miss, but he could be primed to eclipse that number against FSU. item.title: Min Woo Lee’s Missing Eight-Iron Story Is Pure Gold
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Min Woo Lee played well despite a gear malfunction on Thursday. The Australian fired a 68 at the BMW Australian PGA Championship while playing without his eight-iron. In Las Vegas, after a golf lesson with Formula 1 drivers Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll, Lee lost the club. He blamed their hands-on approach for the disappearance. “Funny story, I was with Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll and I was giving them a lesson and I think they were touching the clubs and it’s gone somewhere, so I had no eight-iron,” Lee said. Turning a Loss into a Creative Win Most golfers panic when a key iron vanishes from the bag. They start overthinking every shot from the fairway. He treated the missing club as a fun puzzle to solve. He admitted he needed the eight-iron a few times during the round. “The third hole of the day I needed an eight-iron, I needed it a few times today,” Lee told reporters. Instead of stressing, he adjusted his swing. He hit his nine-iron harder or added spin with his seven-iron to fill the gap. “It’s actually a really fun way to play golf: it’s either a nine iron and I’ve got to hit it harder or add some spin with a seven iron,” he added. The Leaderboard Reality Check Lee sits four strokes behind the shock leader Haydn Barron after the opening round. Barron posted nine birdies, including all par-fives, to card an eight-under 64. That is the lowest round of Barron’s DP World Tour career. Lee’s 68 keeps him in the hunt despite the club shortage. “I felt like I hit really good shots, better shots than I would have with an eight-iron so I wasn’t stressing,” Lee said. The club is reportedly back in Sydney at the house now. Lee might keep it out just to see if he can win without it. The tournament continues Friday with live coverage on Sky Sports .

item.title: Bears Tickets Cost More Than A Used Car For Families
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The days of giving away Chicago Bears tickets are long gone. The team now holds the title of the most expensive ticket in town, or any town. Sports Illustrated reports that the cheapest upper deck seat for the season finale in Minnesota sits between $214.20 and $223.47 on Ticketmaster. That price is just for entry, and it requires flexibility since the league has not set a date or time for that final week game yet. Driving to Detroit for the Thanksgiving game offers a slightly different but still painful price tag. Standing room only tickets cost $238, while end zone upper level seats run $285. WSCR-AM and Ticketdata.com noted that the seven most expensive remaining NFL game tickets are all for Bears games. A family of four trying to attend the rest of the season might need to take out a loan just to get through the turnstiles. The Christmas Price Tag Surprising a child or a spouse with a trip to see Caleb Williams live on Christmas against the Packers is a costly dream. Sports Illustrated states that fans can get in and out for $708.05 per person plus taxes. There are no cheaper tickets available for that game as of Wednesday, Nov. 25. The next home game against Jacksonville offers upper section south end zone seats for $448, but nothing cheaper exists on the market right now. The premium the Bears command as a road opponent is truly staggering. A chart shared by TicketData Keith shows the get-in prices for Miami Dolphins home games, where their game versus the Bills sits at $135. A single upper deck corner seat in the north end zone for the Bears’ penultimate Soldier Field matchup versus the Lions is priced at $466.83. Fans Push Back on Costs Long-time supporters are furious about these numbers. A fan who has followed the team for over 20 years posted on social media asking why it costs over $450 before taxes per ticket. The post, shared by THE ICEMAN & BEN JOHNSON SHOW, questioned how this pricing benefits fans when the cost is so high.

item.title: Xhekaj Fined By NHL Following Violent Game Versus Avalanche
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Montreal Canadien s forward Florian Xhekaj has been fined by the NHL’s Department of Player Safety , following Wednesday night’s violent outing against the Colorado Avalanche. The amount Xhekaj must forfeit is $2,426.98, the maximum allowed under the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement. Montreal’s Florian Xhekaj has been fined $2,426.98, the maximum allowable under the CBA, for a dangerous trip against Colorado’s Fedor Svechkov. — NHL Player Safety (@NHLPlayerSafety) November 26, 2026 The incident occurred in the third period with the game clearly out of reach. Xhekaj received a five-minute match penalty for his actions against Fedor Svechkov. Florian Xhekaj has received a match penalty for an attempt to injure after this slew-foot on Fedor Svechkov 😬 https://t.co/gSfR2Pht9p — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) November 26, 2026 Meltdown In Denver There is no excusing that type of conduct, as slewfoots rank among the most dangerous plays on an NHL rink. In that sense, some would argue Xhekaj was fortunate to avoid a suspension. It should be noted that the NHL did not label the play a slewfoot, describing it instead as a dangerous trip. All things considered, Wednesday night’s 6-0 loss to the Avalanche ranked among the Canadiens’ poorest efforts in recent years, which helps explain the intense frustration that was largely directed at Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog. Earlier in the game, Landeskog delivered a highly questionable hit on Kaiden Guhle that forced the defenceman from the ice and out of the game. Landeskog with a hit that was borderline boarding. Kadri is the only one that walks away with a roughing penalty in the scrum after. #Avs #GoAvsGo https://t.co/aMrXFnQmgM — Hockey Mountain High (@HockeyMtnHighCO) November 26, 2026 The Canadiens were clearly eager for payback, and seeing as they weren’t able to muster any semblance of offence, they sought other outlets. Again, the aim here is not to justify Xhekaj’s actions but to explain how the teams arrived at that point. In addition to Florian Xhekaj’s unsuccessful attempts to goad Landeskog into a fight, his brother Arber also sought retribution, including a cross-check to Nazem Kadri’s face in the third period. Xhekaj gets 2 minutes for high-sticking Kadri. #GoHabsGo https://t.co/D4rJJLvEt0 — Montreal Hockey Now (@MTLhockeynow) November 26, 2026 Unsatisfied with the earlier hit that injured Guhle, Landeskog later poured salt on the wound by suggesting the Xhekaj brothers were embarrassing the Canadiens franchise. Regardless of one’s view on that claim, it is fair to note that Landeskog has been suspended multiple times in the NHL for dirty plays, while neither Florian nor Arber Xhekaj has ever been suspended in their NHL careers. Gabriel Landeskog is trying to lecture other players in the NHL about dirty plays? https://t.co/IarIStuAy1 — /r/Habs (@HabsOnReddit) November 26, 2026 Hypocrisy aside, there is no question the Canadiens were on tilt against the Avalanche
item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Montreal Canadien s forward Florian Xhekaj has been fined by the NHL’s Department of Player Safety , following Wednesday night’s violent outing against the Colorado Avalanche. The amount Xhekaj must forfeit is $2,426.98, the maximum allowed under the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement. Montreal’s Florian Xhekaj has been fined $2,426.98, the maximum allowable under the CBA, for a dangerous trip against Colorado’s Fedor Svechkov. — NHL Player Safety (@NHLPlayerSafety) November 26, 2026 The incident occurred in the third period with the game clearly out of reach. Xhekaj received a five-minute match penalty for his actions against Fedor Svechkov. Florian Xhekaj has received a match penalty for an attempt to injure after this slew-foot on Fedor Svechkov 😬 https://t.co/gSfR2Pht9p — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) November 26, 2026 Meltdown In Denver There is no excusing that type of conduct, as slewfoots rank among the most dangerous plays on an NHL rink. In that sense, some would argue Xhekaj was fortunate to avoid a suspension. It should be noted that the NHL did not label the play a slewfoot, describing it instead as a dangerous trip. All things considered, Wednesday night’s 6-0 loss to the Avalanche ranked among the Canadiens’ poorest efforts in recent years, which helps explain the intense frustration that was largely directed at Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog. Earlier in the game, Landeskog delivered a highly questionable hit on Kaiden Guhle that forced the defenceman from the ice and out of the game. Landeskog with a hit that was borderline boarding. Kadri is the only one that walks away with a roughing penalty in the scrum after. #Avs #GoAvsGo https://t.co/aMrXFnQmgM — Hockey Mountain High (@HockeyMtnHighCO) November 26, 2026 The Canadiens were clearly eager for payback, and seeing as they weren’t able to muster any semblance of offence, they sought other outlets. Again, the aim here is not to justify Xhekaj’s actions but to explain how the teams arrived at that point. In addition to Florian Xhekaj’s unsuccessful attempts to goad Landeskog into a fight, his brother Arber also sought retribution, including a cross-check to Nazem Kadri’s face in the third period. Xhekaj gets 2 minutes for high-sticking Kadri. #GoHabsGo https://t.co/D4rJJLvEt0 — Montreal Hockey Now (@MTLhockeynow) November 26, 2026 Unsatisfied with the earlier hit that injured Guhle, Landeskog later poured salt on the wound by suggesting the Xhekaj brothers were embarrassing the Canadiens franchise. Regardless of one’s view on that claim, it is fair to note that Landeskog has been suspended multiple times in the NHL for dirty plays, while neither Florian nor Arber Xhekaj has ever been suspended in their NHL careers. Gabriel Landeskog is trying to lecture other players in the NHL about dirty plays? https://t.co/IarIStuAy1 — /r/Habs (@HabsOnReddit) November 26, 2026 Hypocrisy aside, there is no question the Canadiens were on tilt against the Avalanche, a situation that cannot be repeated moving forward. Jake Evans after the Habs loss tonight: “There’s a time and a place I guess, but I think emotionally we need to show our maturity, instead of unraveling and being frustrated.” “We got pretty frustrated after certain events and then it unraveled from there.” https://t.co/B9I6c5T9od — /r/Habs (@HabsOnReddit) November 26, 2026 Related Headlines Maple Leafs Make Significant Changes To Power Play With Marchenko Return Chicago Blackhawks May Have Already Found Connor Bedard’s Long-Term Running Mate Habs Daily: Demidov Nearing Return, Larkin Trade Narrative, Guhle Injury Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Thanksgiving in Paradise for WVU Women’s Basketball
item.description: Photo by Trystan Layton While most of us will be spending Thanksgiving eating way too much food, the West Virginia women’s basketball team will be spending the holiday in the Bahamas. I would say they got the better end of that deal. The No. 22 Mountaineers enter the Battle 4 Atlantis with a 5-0 record and two big matchups against Florida and No. 13 Notre Dame. Coming off a 98-60 win over Akron last Tuesday, West Virginia will have its work cut out for it this week. The Mountaineers will first take on Florida, which enters the matchup with a 4-2 record. The Gators are led by Kiyomi McMiller, who is averaging 24 points per game. Things will not get any easier on Thanksgiving morning when West Virginia takes on Notre Dame. The Fighting Irish also entered the week undefeated and are led by Hannah Hidalgo, who is averaging an impressive 28.8 points per game. With 10 newcomers on the roster this season, Mark Kellogg’s team has already shown that it can find ways to win. However, these next two games will be a good test for the Mountaineers and give us a better idea of what to expect from this team moving forward. Picking up two wins in the Bahamas would be huge for West Virginia, especially with Big 12 play right around the corner. The Mountaineers will face Florida on Tuesday at 3:30 p.m. on ESPN+ before taking on Notre Dame on Thanksgiving morning at 11:30 a.m. on ESPN2. So, if you are looking for something to watch while waiting for Thanksgiving dinner, the Mountaineers have you covered. Hopefully, they will give us something extra to be thankful for!

item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic Sends Heartfelt Thanksgiving Note to JJ Redick
item.description: Luka Doncic #77 hugs head coach JJ Redick of the Los Angeles Lakers against the Dallas Mavericks during the fourth quarter at American Airlines Center on April 09, 2025 in Dallas, Texas. Getty Historically great NBA teams are built on a strong bond between the head coach and the franchise star — a box the new-era Los Angeles Lakers seem to have checked with JJ Redick and Luka Doncic. Their bond dates back to their days as Dallas Mavericks teammates and has only grown stronger since shifting to a player-coach dynamic. On Thanksgiving Eve, Doncic posted an Instagram Story standing side-by-side with Redick, set to Randy Newman’s “You’ve Got a Friend in Me.” JJ Redick Trusts Luka Doncic In his second full season coaching Doncic, Redick has granted the Slovenian autonomy — not only to run the offense, but to change plays on the fly and act as his extension on the floor. Redick also fully supports Doncic vocal leadership, which was on full display last Friday against the Sacramento Kings when cameras caught him cussing out Sandro Mamukelashvili for repeatedly getting blown past on defense. While the public outburst drew some criticism, Redick stood firmly behind his star player. “First of all, I think that what he’s been doing has been great, because he’s leading not out of frustration,” Redick said of Doncic’s leadership. “…Those guys have been awesome and Luka has been leading that. They are problem-solving in real time,” he added, praising Doncic for holding teammates accountable. Lakers vs Spurs NBA Cup Coming off a rare four-night in-season break, the Lakers return to action Friday against the San Antonio Spurs in a heavyweight NBA Cup group-stage finale. The high-stakes matchup could determine which team advances to the knockouts. Entering Friday, four West teams — the Lakers, Spurs, Trail Blazers and Warriors — sit tied at 2-1. While Los Angeles must beat San Antonio to keep any realistic quarterfinal hopes alive, the Spurs hold the tiebreaker edge thanks to a league-leading point differential. Friday’s clash with the Spurs will be the first true test for the Lakers, who have played the league’s second-easiest schedule through the opening month. It marks their first matchup against a top-six West seed, kicking off a tough three-game stretch that includes games against the Houston Rockets and Memphis Grizzlies. Redick admits the next week will reveal if his Lakers are legit. “I think these four games will be a great barometer of where we’re at,” Redick said on Wednesday, via ESPN’s Dave McMenamin. “…And whether we lose the game, whether we win the game, we’re either going to be contenders on ‘First Take’ or we’re not going to be contenders and we’re fake. That stuff is just noise. We’re going to focus on the process of trying to get better and it’s a good test to see where we’re at,” he added. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Lakers’ Luka Doncic Sends Heartfelt Thanksgiving Note to JJ Redick appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: 'Steelers organization is the one who deserves the most blame': Mina Kimes lays blame for Rodgers-McCarthy fallout
item.description: Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images, The Mina Kimes Show Hindsight is 20/20, but is anyone actually surprised that the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy reunion ended in disaster? ESPN’s Mina Kimes certainly isn’t, and she thinks the Pittsburgh Steelers should have known better. Rodgers and McCarthy worked well together in Green Bay until they didn’t, and it was understood that bad blood developed between them. On paper, the two put aside their differences this offseason when the Steelers hired McCarthy to oversee what was presumed to be Rodgers’ final NFL season. That lasted all of 10 games before the Steelers released a shocking statement late Tuesday night announcing Rodgers had not only been benched but also wouldn’t play in this week’s game. The next day, Rodgers went scorched earth on The Pat McAfee Show , accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep during team meetings, alluding to the Steelers’ head coach struggling to keep up with the rigors of coaching an NFL team, noting that McCarthy held a grudge against him from how things ended in Green Bay, and much more. The Steelers released Rodgers following that interview while McCarthy danced around the accusations to explain why he’s still the right guy for the job. Reports suggest Rodgers issued an ultimatum over play-calling responsibilities , and McCarthy took him at his word, leading to Rodgers being benched. Opinions about the breakup have been intense, with some blaming Rodgers and others blaming McCarthy . ESPN’s Mina Kimes thinks there’s another entity ultimately at fault for how this played out: the Pittsburgh Steelers. On Thursday’s episode of The Mina Kimes Show , the ESPN NFL analyst said that despite Rodgers’ protestations, it’s obvious that this was a “marriage of inconvenience of two people who clearly hated each other” from the beginning, as neither man was getting much attention from the rest of the league. Now the players are paying the price as they try to keep fighting for a playoff spot amid a media circus. For that, Kimes lays the blame at the organization’s feet. “The Steelers organization is the one who deserves the most blame. The front office and ownership,” said Kimes. “It was all so god damn predictable. That’s what I’ll say. Everybody was shocked when this reunion happened cause we all knew they didn’t like each other.” Kimes also pointed out that “the football was also very predictable,” and the Steelers offense has struggled, with Rodgers putting up league-worst numbers. “It’s not like the Steelers didn’t know any of this,” she continued. “They made a terrible football decision, but also a terrible people management decision. And they, to me, deserve more blame than anyone in all this. “This was a disaster entirely of their own making. item.title: Tevez hopes Ronaldo will join Messi at testimonial
item.description: Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo may play alongside Lionel Messi in Carlos Tevez's testimonial (RONALDO SCHEMIDT) Former Argentina striker Carlos Tevez said Thursday Lionel Messi would appear in his testimonial next month and that he was confident Cristiano Ronaldo would be playing alongside them. The 42-year-old Tevez played with Messi for Argentina and also lined up with Ronaldo at Manchester United. Tevez started his career at Boca Juniors and returned there in 2018 before retiring four years later, and now his testimonial will be played December 20 at their Bombonera stadium in Buenos Aires. Messi, 39, and 41-year-old Ronaldo have faced off against each other many times on the pitch, notably in several El Clasico fixtures during their respective times at Barcelona and Real Madrid. If Tevez succeeds in luring the Portuguese forward to the Bombonera, it could be the first time ever that the pair who marked their generation play on the same side. Other illustrious footballers scheduled for the match are the Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, Argentine midfielder Juan Roman Riquelme and former England centre-back Rio Ferdinand. mry/sa/dmc/nf

item.title: Journalist: Liverpool set to green light January move for striker
item.description: Journalist: Liverpool set to green light January move for striker Liverpool Transfer News: David Lynch Reveals January Loan Plans for Will Wright Liverpool forward Will Wright continues to impress at academy level, with his performances in the UEFA Youth League prompting discussion about the next stage of his development. Speaking on the Media Matters podcast for Anfield Index, David Lynch and Dave Davis discussed the youngster’s future, Liverpool’s attacking options and the possibility of a January loan departure. Wright’s impressive goalscoring record has generated calls from some Liverpool supporters for him to receive opportunities in the first team. Both contributors, however, identified regular exposure to senior football as an important step in his progression. Lynch also revealed that Liverpool are considering sending the talented forward out on loan during the January transfer window. Will Wright Impressing in UEFA Youth League Davis highlighted Wright’s impressive attacking output in European competition, with the Liverpool youngster registering eight goals and two assists in four UEFA Youth League appearances. His performances have prompted questions about whether he should receive opportunities under Andoni Iraola, particularly given the frequency with which he is producing goals at academy level. Davis questioned whether remaining in youth football would provide Wright with the necessary challenge to continue developing. “He needs men’s football, surely,” Davis stated. “If he’s going to develop or go to the next stage, surely it’s men’s football for him.” Lynch was in complete agreement with that assessment, highlighting Wright’s performances across Liverpool’s academy competitions. “He is finding it too easy in youth football. His numbers in the Premier League Two are pretty good as well this season.” For Lynch, Wright’s performances indicate that the youngster is ready to be tested in a more demanding environment. Liverpool Attacking Options Limit First Team Opportunities Competition for places within Liverpool’s forward line featured prominently in the discussion between Davis and Lynch. Alexander Isak, the presence of Koumas and the impending return of Hugo Ekitike were among the factors referenced by Lynch when assessing Wright’s immediate prospects of senior involvement. Davis also highlighted the performances of Liverpool’s established attacking players. “Liverpool’s first team forward line has never been more competitive. Speaking on the Media Matters podcast for Anfield Index, David Lynch and Dave Davis discussed the youngster’s future, Liverpool’s attacking options and the possibility of a January loan departure. Wright’s impressive goalscoring record has generated calls from some Liverpool supporters for him to receive opportunities in the first team. Both contributors, however, identified regular exposure to senior football as an important step in his progression. Lynch also revealed that Liverpool are considering sending the talented forward out on loan during the January transfer window. Will Wright Impressing in UEFA Youth League Davis highlighted Wright’s impressive attacking output in European competition, with the Liverpool youngster registering eight goals and two assists in four UEFA Youth League appearances. His performances have prompted questions about whether he should receive opportunities under Andoni Iraola, particularly given the frequency with which he is producing goals at academy level. Davis questioned whether remaining in youth football would provide Wright with the necessary challenge to continue developing. “He needs men’s football, surely,” Davis stated. “If he’s going to develop or go to the next stage, surely it’s men’s football for him.” Lynch was in complete agreement with that assessment, highlighting Wright’s performances across Liverpool’s academy competitions. “He is finding it too easy in youth football. His numbers in the Premier League Two are pretty good as well this season.” For Lynch, Wright’s performances indicate that the youngster is ready to be tested in a more demanding environment. Liverpool Attacking Options Limit First Team Opportunities Competition for places within Liverpool’s forward line featured prominently in the discussion between Davis and Lynch. Alexander Isak, the presence of Koumas and the impending return of Hugo Ekitike were among the factors referenced by Lynch when assessing Wright’s immediate prospects of senior involvement. Davis also highlighted the performances of Liverpool’s established attacking players. “Liverpool’s first team forward line has never been more competitive. Look how well it’s doing.” Lynch questioned how many meaningful opportunities Wright would realistically receive, including in domestic cup competitions. “It’s very difficult to see Will Wright, even in the League Cup, getting minutes.” The journalist acknowledged that occasional substitute appearances might be possible for the youngster, questioning how beneficial those opportunities would be for his development. “Maybe he could get ten minutes at the end of it or something like that. But, you know, that’s not going to massively develop him.” The strength of Liverpool’s attacking options formed a significant part of Lynch’s reasoning for advocating a temporary departure. Photo: IMAGO January Loan Under Consideration for Will Wright Perhaps the most significant information from Lynch concerned Liverpool’s plans for the upcoming January transfer window. “I think a loan is an absolute must for him,” Lynch explained. The journalist subsequently revealed that Liverpool are already considering that possibility. “The suggestion is that Liverpool are looking at that, as I understand it. It’s under consideration.” Lynch emphasised the importance of Wright experiencing the physical demands of senior football, where playing against experienced defenders would present a fresh challenge. “I think it will be the right move for everyone to get him out there and get him kind of roughed up by some grisly defenders and learn from that.” Liverpool have yet to make a definitive decision, according to Lynch’s assessment, although the journalist was clear about his preferred outcome. Continuing to dominate academy opposition every week, in his view, would offer diminishing developmental benefits for the young forward. Lynch concluded with an assessment that reflected both his appreciation of Wright’s performances and his desire to see the Liverpool prospect challenged further. “He’s been brilliant. Now it’s time to move him up and test him.”

item.title: Van Dijk, Mac Allister and Ngumoha To Start | 4-2-3-1 Liverpool Predicted Lineup Vs Everton
item.description: Van Dijk, Mac Allister and Ngumoha To Start | 4-2-3-1 Liverpool Predicted Lineup Vs Everton Liverpool will face off against Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium this Sunday as they look to secure a good result on the road in the Merseyside club. The Reds managed to earn an impressive 3-0 win away at Club Brugge recently, which should keep them in good spirits going into this game. Andoni Iraola will set his side up in a 4-2-3-1 formation and is expected to make some tweaks to his first team for this clash. Virgil Van Dijk, Alexis Mac Allister and Rio Ngumoha could all play from the start of this game. 4-2-3-1 Liverpool Predicted Lineup To Face Everton Defence Alisson Becker will operate in goal for the Reds after he secured a clean sheet in his last appearance. Jeremy Jacquet will function alongside Virgil Van Dijk at the heart of the Liverpool backline as they look to keep the opposition attackers frustrated throughout the game. Ronald Araujo will try to prove his worth as the right-back, while Milos Kerkez hopes to put in a good display on the other flank as the left-back. Both of them will get the freedom to go forward and join in on the attack at every chance they can get. Joe Gomez will offer cover for the defensive positions on the bench. BRUGES, BELGIUM – NOVEMBER 25: Bradley Barcola of Liverpool reacts after a missed chance during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Club Brugge KV and Liverpool FC at Jan Breydel Stadium on November 25, 2026 in Bruges, Belgium. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) Midfield Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister will anchor the midfield for the Merseyside club as they focus on winning the 50-50 battles in the middle of the park and engineering some clear-cut chances in the final third. The talented trio of Rio Ngumoha, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola will play just ahead of them as part of Iraola’s attack. All three of them need to be at the top of their game if the Reds are to secure a convincing win in the Merseyside derby this weekend. Victor Munoz and Ryan Gravenberch are both major doubts for this game. However, Trey Nyoni and Jeremie Frimpong will be named on the bench and might come on to make an impact in the second half if required. Attack Alexander Isak will spearhead Liverpool’s attack up top. He would be keen on finding the back of the net after scoring a brace in midweek. Lewis Koumas will be available for selection on the bench as he waits for his chance to influence the game in the latter stages if needed.

Lewis Koumas will be available for selection on the bench as he waits for his chance to influence the game in the latter stages if needed.

item.title: Referee being 'drunk' claims are 'entirely unfounded'
item.description: Hanna Hattab has refereed in a number of competitions run by the Asian Football Confederation [Getty Images] Claims that a referee was drunk during an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match are "entirely unfounded", officials say. Syrian referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time of the match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates. Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following what has been described as some erratic decision-making in the first half. Iranian news agency ISNA quoted one club official as saying: "The referee was not in a normal state," and suggesting they would not have played on had the referee not been removed. Accusations of drunkenness were also widely shared on social media. But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has released a statement denying the allegation, saying he has been defamed and threatening legal action. The fourth official took over for the second half, with Al Jazira winning the match. Hattab said he will be "issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened". Omani sports journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian competitions, claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus". "He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating." In their statement on the match, which was played in Asia's second tier continental competition, the Syrian Football Association backed Hattab. "Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media - that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded," they wrote. "The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident." item.title: Who is to blame for Ohio State’s disappointing season?
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith's helmet sits on the sideline as the team warms up prior to the NCAA football game against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign on Oct. 11, 2025. For the first time in recent memory, an Ohio State season is effectively over before Thanksgiving. The Buckeyes are 7–4, coming off a loss to Nebraska, ranked No. 21 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. The Buckeyes’ upcoming game against the Michigan Wolverines, who are also having an extremely disappointing season, has none of the buzz or stakes that usually come with “The Game.” OSU’s season begs the question: How did a season with national championship expectations quickly turn into a complete collapse? Arthur Smith hasn’t fixed the offense Hiring Arthur Smith was supposed to bring an NFL perspective and a fresh identity to an offense that needed revitalization. Instead, the results have been underwhelming. The offense lacks rhythm, creativity, and a consistent identity. Too often, it feels like a collection of talented players rather than a coordinated unit. The running game has been a major problem. Bo Jackson has not lived up to the expectations surrounding his return, and the depth behind him has done little to provide a boost. The offensive line hasn’t played up to the standard either. That leaves too much pressure on Julian Sayin, Luke Fahey, and the passing game. Sayin’s season-ending arm injury, which he suffered against the Indiana Hoosiers, has only made matters worse. He wasn’t playing his best football before going down, but asking Fahey, a true freshman backup, to operate an inconsistent offense against quality competition was never going to be an easy transition. Then there’s Jeremiah Smith, who is arguably the best player in program history. As good as Smith is, force-feeding him when defenses are already focused on taking him away has made the offense predictable. The defense got too much credit Matt Patricia’s defense looked dominant last season, but how much of that success belonged to the coordinator and how much came from the players executing his system? Sonny Styles and Arvell Reese were elite, and Caleb Downs was one of the best defensive players in college football. With those players in the NFL now, the defense has looked considerably less intimidating. The pass rush has been particularly dismal. Ohio State has recorded just 16 sacks this season, and opposing quarterbacks haven’t had enough reason to fear pressure. Watching Kenyatta Jackson drop into coverage while the defense struggles to generate a consistent rush raises legitimate questions about the scheme. There are also personnel decisions worth questioning. Peyton Pierce continues to receive significant playing time despite inconsistent results, while younger players appear capable of providing more. Tim Walton’s secondary has also struggled to replicate last year’s standard. Ryan Day owns the lion’s share of the blame Coaching

Bo Jackson has not lived up to the expectations surrounding his return, and the depth behind him has done little to provide a boost. The offensive line hasn’t played up to the standard either. That leaves too much pressure on Julian Sayin, Luke Fahey, and the passing game. Sayin’s season-ending arm injury, which he suffered against the Indiana Hoosiers, has only made matters worse. He wasn’t playing his best football before going down, but asking Fahey, a true freshman backup, to operate an inconsistent offense against quality competition was never going to be an easy transition. Then there’s Jeremiah Smith, who is arguably the best player in program history. As good as Smith is, force-feeding him when defenses are already focused on taking him away has made the offense predictable. There are also personnel decisions worth questioning. Peyton Pierce continues to receive significant playing time despite inconsistent results, while younger players appear capable of providing more. Tim Walton’s secondary has also struggled to replicate last year’s standard. Ryan Day owns the lion’s share of the blame Coaching continuity matters in college football, especially when recruiting relationships and player development are involved, but continuity can’t become an excuse for keeping coaches who aren’t getting the job done. Day has to own the decisions to retain and empower this staff. He also has to answer for a staff and team that continues to look tight in its biggest games, which is a recurring theme during his tenure. The 2024 championship run showed what this program can accomplish when everything clicks, but one magical postseason doesn’t erase the questions that have followed Day throughout his career. item.title: Football Daily | Bayern Munich go from bad to worse with own goals on and off the pitch
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Champions League review: Lille monster Bayern, De Bruyne’s sad return and more United chaos
item.description: The French side earned their first group win over troubled German giants as Bellingham and Betis also caught the eye Bayern Munich have hit a snagging point, with injuries wracking Vincent Kompany’s squad just as the head coach returns to work following his own health scare. For Lille’s winner, to exact Bayern’s first loss of the season, Aleksandar Pavlović had an own goal for the ages, desperately chasing back to then somehow direct the ball into his own net. Bayern are 15th in the Champions League table, and with Harry Kane out until well into 2027 and 18-year-old Lennart Karl asked to lead the line, resources are stretched. Jamal Musiala, subject of club grandees Uli Hoeness and Karl Heinz-Rummenigge’s gripes over his contract in the light of his neurological condition, could also play only 15 minutes. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We are on the edge’: how Swedish league declined from summit of women’s game
item.description: The Damallsvenskan once mastered Europe and attracted the best players, but many are now worried for its future On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes. It was a bitter pill to swallow but there was still the belief that the tournament would mark the start of women’s football’s commercial breakthrough in Sweden. After all, how could sponsors and broadcasters ignore such undeniable interest? Continue reading...

item.title: Neville, Carragher and the inescapable podcasting feedback loop of doom | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Even the best managers can struggle to escape ex-players’ need to manufacture a crisis for content. Enter Michael Carrick … A podcast studio in Manchester. A production runner pours water into jugs. Gary Neville enters the room with Michael Carrick. Neville: Just so you know, we’re already filming. This is the intro bit, where we show everyone coming on to set and doing some light banter. It humanises us. The viewer sees it and thinks we’re just mates chatting about football, rather than scions of a global podcast empire commercially obliged to produce an endless scroll of provocative content for money. I always say: why can’t you be both? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Not Bayern-like’: Joshua Kimmich fumes at club’s treatment of Jamal Musiala
item.description: Bundesliga champions lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday Kimmich defends Musiala’s neurological condition The Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club’s “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures. Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala’s performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in pre-season games, drawing protests from the players’ union Fifpro. Now Kimmich, the club’s vice-captain, has spoken out and warned Bayern risked undermining their family image. Continue reading...

item.title: No drums, no tifo … no point? The impact of Palace’s missing Holmesdale Fanatics
item.description: Crystal Palace’s influential supporters’ group disbanded 24 hours before their first home game this season – and Selhurst Park has not been the same since Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket. “Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.” Continue reading...

item.title: Peter Storey obituary
item.description: Arsenal midfielder capped by England 19 times whose life after football suffered a drink-fuelled decline The footballer Peter Storey , who has died aged 81, was a tough-tackling midfielder for Arsenal when they won the double of the First Division championship and the FA Cup in 1971. Arsenal were only the fourth team to achieve the double at that point (it has since been won another nine times), and Storey, who appeared in 49 of the 51 league and FA Cup games that season, played as big a role as anyone in securing the honours with his defensive solidity, ball-winning skills, “good engine”, sound distribution and reliable occasional penalty taking. Continue reading...

item.title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester City get that empty feeling as they fail to win again
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners. In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change . ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis. May I be the 1,092nd correspondent to demand a review of the Letter o’ the Day award for Monday – and it be awarded to Declan Hackett for his letter foretelling the rescinding of the red card given to Lenny Yoro on Sunday? Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to fiasco but issues do not stop there | Osasu Obayiuwana
item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. Continue reading...

item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: John Duerden
item.content:encoded: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | The game’s gone: has fantasy football been ruined by AI gafferbots?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago . If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [ Monday’s Football Daily ], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David ” – Ronnie McMahon. Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [ Monday’s letters ] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan. In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski ” – Nigel Sanders. Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others). Continue reading...

item.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
item.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says. Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 . “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Esposito emulates Vieri with Inter hat-trick but De Ketelaere haunts him again
item.description: Italy’s new cover star enjoyed a ‘beautiful’ treble but could not celebrate it after his side threw away two-goal leads three times to draw 4-4 with Atalanta This ought to have been a magic moment for Pio Esposito. He had just scored his first Serie A hat-trick, becoming only the third Italian to get one for Inter in the era of three points for a win. The last to do it was Christian Vieri, back in 2003. Two years before Esposito was born. We will come back to that. Esposito has been drawing premature comparisons to Vieri for some time and especially now after a barnstorming November in which he has scored eight times in five games, including three in two for his country, and two of those as part of a man-of-the-match performance during an upset win against France . item.title: Jamal Musiala controversy the nadir of Bayern Munich’s turbulent week
item.description: German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat. The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are rocking the Premier League elite. But can they mount a title tilt?

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...
